exercises.name: Quad Sets
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with BOTH legs fully extended straight along the ground, a small rolled towel under one knee. The quadriceps on one leg is visibly flexed and tight. Arms resting at sides, toes pointing up.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with both legs fully extended; the working leg's quadriceps is maximally contracted and visibly hardened, with the knee held in full extension and the foot pointed upward, while the towel roll remains under the knee; the non-working leg stays relaxed and flat on the ground, and the arms remain at rest at the sides.

exercises.name: Straight Leg Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one knee bent and foot flat on the floor for support. The other leg is lifted straight off the ground to approximately 45 degrees with the knee fully locked and toes pointed toward the ceiling. Arms rest at sides, and the lower back maintains contact with the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lying flat on the back on the ground, face up. The left knee is bent with foot flat on the floor. The right leg is raised straight up to approximately 45 degrees from the floor with the knee fully locked.

exercises.name: Wall Sits
exercises.pose_description: Doing a wall sit exercise: back flat against a wall, knees bent at 90 degrees in a deep squat, thighs parallel to the floor, like sitting in an invisible chair. Feet flat on the floor shoulder-width apart. Arms at sides. The hips are at the same height as the knees, NOT on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains stationary in an isometric deep squat position with their back firmly pressed against the wall, knees bent at 90 degrees, thighs parallel to the ground, and feet shoulder-width apart on the floor. Their hips are held level with their knees, creating the appearance of sitting in an invisible chair, with arms resting at their sides or crossed over their chest. The quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles are visibly tensed and engaged as they hold this contracted position against gravity.

exercises.name: Clamshells
exercises.pose_description: Side-lying hip exercise. The man is on his side like a sleeping position, facing the viewer. Head propped on bottom arm. Both knees are bent. The top leg's knee is raised up toward the ceiling while feet stay together. View from front showing the side-lying body clearly.
exercises.end_pose_description: Lying on the left side on the ground. Both knees are bent at about 45 degrees. Feet are stacked together and remain touching. The top (right) knee is lifted and opened up toward the ceiling at maximum abduction, like a clamshell opening.

exercises.name: Heel Slides
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back, viewed from the side. One leg is straight on the ground. The other knee is bent with the foot flat on the floor near the buttocks, heel touching the ground. Arms at sides.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back, with the bent knee fully extended straight along the floor, heel still in contact with the ground, creating a long line from hip to foot. The quadriceps and hip flexors appear visibly engaged and contracted as the leg reaches full extension. The opposite leg remains straight on the floor, arms stay at sides, and the torso remains flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Step-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright facing a low step or platform approximately 6 to 8 inches high. One foot is placed entirely on the step, and the body is driven upward by pressing through that foot until standing tall on the step with both feet. Arms may be at sides or held at the waist for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands fully upright on the elevated step platform with both feet planted side-by-side, knees extended and legs straight, torso erect and shoulders back. The quadriceps, glutes, and calf muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, with the entire body weight supported on the elevated surface. Arms are positioned at the sides or waist for balance, and the person faces forward in a stable, neutral standing position.

exercises.name: Pendulum Swings
exercises.pose_description: Standing with feet shoulder-width apart, bending forward at the waist approximately 45 to 60 degrees. The non-working arm rests on a table or chair for support. The affected arm hangs straight down like a pendulum and swings gently in small circles or back and forth, completely relaxed with no active muscle contraction.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing next to a table with the left hand resting on it for support. The upper body is bent forward at the hips at about 45 degrees. The right arm hangs freely and has swung forward to the front of its arc, extended in front of the body.

exercises.name: External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, elbow pinned to the side of the body. A resistance band or light dumbbell is held in the hand. The forearm rotates outward away from the body while keeping the elbow firmly against the torso, moving through approximately 45 degrees of external rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with the working arm still bent 90 degrees at the elbow, pinned against the ribcage, but the forearm is rotated outward away from the centerline of the body at approximately 45 degrees. The forearm appears nearly perpendicular to the body's sagittal plane, with visible tension in the shoulder and upper back muscles, particularly the posterior deltoid and rotator cuff, while the opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side.

exercises.name: Scapular Squeezes
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with good posture, shoulders relaxed and arms at sides. The shoulder blades are actively squeezed together toward the spine, pulling the shoulders back and opening the chest. The chin is slightly tucked and the head remains in a neutral position throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright. The shoulder blades are squeezed maximally together behind the back. The chest is pushed forward and open. The shoulders are pulled back. Both arms are at the sides with elbows slightly bent.

exercises.name: Wall Slides
exercises.pose_description: Standing with back flat against a wall. Both arms are raised in a goalpost or W shape with elbows bent at 90 degrees, backs of hands and forearms touching the wall. Feet are close to the wall. This is NOT a pull-up — there is no bar. The person is standing against a flat wall with arms in a W shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing with back flat against a wall. Both arms are raised fully overhead with elbows straight, hands and forearms still touching the wall. Arms in a Y position above the head. Shoulders fully flexed.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position, wrists under shoulders, knees under hips. The spine is arched upward like a cat, rounding toward the ceiling, head tucked down. Wearing a gray t-shirt and dark shorts.
exercises.end_pose_description: The spine is fully extended and arched downward like a cow, with the chest pushed forward and upward toward the ceiling, shoulders dropped away from ears, and the head tilted back to gaze upward. The arms remain straight with elbows locked, wrists directly under shoulders, while the knees stay bent at 90 degrees under the hips, and the lower back and abdominal muscles appear fully engaged and stretched. The person's gaze is directed upward and slightly behind them.

exercises.name: Glute Bridges
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms resting at sides. Hips are lifted high off the ground forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, with glutes fully squeezed at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with knees bent at 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, hips thrust upward to create a straight diagonal line from knees through torso to shoulders. The glutes are maximally contracted and appear prominently rounded, the core is visibly engaged and tight, and the arms rest flat on the ground alongside the body for stability. The person's gaze points upward toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Bird Dog
exercises.pose_description: Balancing on the left hand and right knee. The RIGHT arm reaches straight out in front, parallel to the ground, and the LEFT leg extends straight behind, also parallel to the ground. The body forms a straight line from fingertips to toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: On all fours in a tabletop position on the ground. The right arm is extended fully forward, parallel to the ground. The left leg is extended fully backward, parallel to the ground. The back is flat and level. Only the left hand and right knee remain on the ground.

exercises.name: Pelvic Tilts
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor hip-width apart. The lower back is gently pressed into the floor by engaging the abdominal muscles and tilting the pelvis posteriorly, flattening the natural lumbar curve. Arms rest at sides and shoulders remain relaxed on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, but the pelvis is maximally tilted posteriorly, causing the lower back to press firmly into the floor with no visible gap between the lumbar spine and the ground. The abdominal muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, the ribcage appears slightly depressed toward the pelvis, and the lower abdomen shows defined tension as the core is fully activated. The person faces directly upward with shoulders relaxed and arms at their sides.

exercises.name: Child's Pose
exercises.pose_description: A yoga child's pose: sitting back on the heels with the body folded completely forward and down, forehead on the ground, arms extended straight forward along the floor. The back is rounded and the person looks like they are bowing down.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is fully folded forward in a deep forward bend, with the forehead resting on the ground and the torso collapsed over the thighs. The knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees with the buttocks sitting back toward the heels, while both arms extend straight forward along the floor with palms down, creating an elongated line from the hips through the fingertips. The entire spine appears rounded and stretched, with the shoulders relaxed and drawn downward, and the gaze directed downward toward the ground.

exercises.name: Doorway Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a doorway facing through it. Both arms are raised to shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees, forearms pressed against each side of the door frame. The body leans forward through the doorway to stretch the chest. One foot is slightly ahead of the other.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in the doorway with both arms raised to shoulder height, elbows bent at 90 degrees with forearms pressed firmly against the door frame on either side, while the torso leans forward through the opening with the chest stretched and shoulders pulled back slightly. The legs remain in a staggered stance with one foot forward, the back straight or slightly arched as the body extends into the stretch. The face looks forward through the doorway, with visible tension across the chest, shoulders, and anterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Hamstring Curls
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or counter for balance. One foot is lifted behind the body by bending the knee, bringing the heel toward the buttock while keeping the thighs parallel. The standing leg remains straight with a slight knee bend, and the torso stays upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains nearly straight with minimal knee bend, while the working leg's knee is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled as close as possible to the glutes, creating a sharp angle at the knee joint. The torso remains upright and vertical, facing forward with the person still gripping the chair/counter for stability, and the hamstring and glute muscles of the lifted leg are visibly contracted and engaged.

exercises.name: Gentle Stretching
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet shoulder-width apart. Both arms are raised straight overhead with fingers interlaced, palms facing the ceiling, stretching tall. Wearing a gray t-shirt and dark shorts. White background.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is gently leaned to one side with the interlaced hands stretched overhead and slightly back, creating a visible elongation along the entire side body from the hip to the fingertips. The feet remain planted shoulder-width apart on the ground, legs straight but not locked, and the head follows the natural curve of the spine in a neutral position. The lateral core, obliques, and shoulder muscles show subtle engagement as the stretch deepens.

exercises.name: Walking
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with good posture, chin level, shoulders relaxed, and arms swinging naturally at sides. One foot is stepping forward in a natural heel-to-toe gait pattern, with the opposite arm swinging forward for counterbalance. The core is engaged and the gaze is directed forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures one leg fully extended behind the body with the heel lifting off the ground, while the opposite leg is forward with the knee slightly bent and foot about to make contact with the ground. The arm opposite to the forward leg is swung forward to shoulder height for momentum, while the other arm swings back, with the torso remaining upright and core visibly engaged. The head stays level and forward-facing with a natural gaze direction.

exercises.name: Seated Hamstring Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Sitting on the ground (NOT on a chair or bench) with one leg extended straight forward. The other knee is bent to the side. The person bends forward at the waist reaching both hands toward the foot of the straight leg to stretch the hamstring.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated on the ground with their torso folded forward at approximately 45-90 degrees toward an extended straight leg, hands clasped or reaching toward the foot/shin of the extended leg, while the opposite leg remains bent with knee out to the side. The extended leg is fully straight with minimal knee bend, the hamstring and calf muscles appear elongated and engaged, and the spine shows flexion as the person leans deeply into the stretch.

exercises.name: Standing Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or chair for balance. Both heels are raised off the floor as high as possible by pushing up onto the balls of the feet, fully contracting the calf muscles. The body remains tall and straight with knees extended.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on the balls of both feet with heels elevated several inches off the ground, ankles plantarflexed at maximum height, while knees remain fully extended and legs are straight. The calves are visibly contracted and bulging, the torso is vertical and stable, and the person lightly grips a wall or chair for balance with one or both hands.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with light support from a chair or wall for balance. The opposite foot is lifted slightly off the ground and the ankle draws slow, controlled circles in the air, moving through full dorsiflexion, inversion, plantarflexion, and eversion. The knee of the circling leg remains relatively still.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on one leg with a slight forward lean, hand lightly touching a chair or wall for balance, while the lifted foot completes a full circular motion with the ankle fully plantarflexed (toes pointed downward) and the leg turned inward in eversion, creating maximum ankle mobility. The supporting leg is nearly straight with a slight knee bend, the torso remains stable and squared forward, and the calf and anterior tibialis muscles appear engaged as the ankle reaches the bottom-most arc of its circular path.

exercises.name: Towel Curls
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and a small towel laid flat beneath the toes. The toes scrunch and grip the towel, pulling it toward the heel in a curling motion. The heel remains firmly on the floor throughout, and the ankle does not move — only the toes actively work to gather the towel.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright in the chair with feet flat on the floor, but the towel is now bunched and gathered in a tight pile beneath the toes and ball of the foot, with the toes fully curled and gripping the compressed towel. The heel stays planted on the floor while the forefoot and toes show maximum flexion and contraction, with visible tension in the intrinsic foot muscles and anterior tibialis. The legs, torso, and head remain completely stationary, with all visible effort concentrated in the intensely curled toe position.

exercises.name: Ankle Alphabet
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg or seated with one leg crossed over the other. The foot of the elevated leg traces the letters of the alphabet in the air using ankle movements only, moving through all planes of motion. The lower leg remains still while the foot moves deliberately through each letter shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg is slightly bent at the knee with the hip engaged, while the elevated leg is extended with the foot positioned at the furthest point of completing a letter (typically with the ankle in plantarflexion, inversion, or eversion depending on which letter is being traced). The torso remains upright and stable, facing forward, with the core visibly engaged to maintain balance as the foot holds its extended position at the endpoint of the current letter's trajectory.

exercises.name: Single Leg Balance
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft, not locked. The opposite foot is lifted a few inches off the ground with the knee bent. Arms can be at sides or extended for balance, torso is upright, and the gaze is directed forward at a fixed point.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands vertically balanced on one leg with a slightly bent knee, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the thigh parallel to the ground. The torso remains upright and centered over the standing leg, with visible core engagement, while the arms are either extended outward at shoulder height or positioned for counterbalance, and the head faces forward with eyes fixed on a point ahead.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Eversion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with a resistance band looped around the outside of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point on the opposite side. The foot pushes outward against the band resistance, turning the sole of the foot away from the midline of the body. The lower leg remains stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle joint.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally turned outward (everted), with the sole of the foot facing laterally away from the body's midline, while the knee remains straight and the lower leg stays stationary. The resistance band is fully stretched, pulling against the outer edge of the forefoot, and the lateral ankle and peroneal muscles along the outer shin appear visibly engaged and contracted.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Ankle Inversion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with a resistance band looped around the inside of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point on the same side. The foot pulls inward against the band resistance, turning the sole of the foot toward the midline of the body. The lower leg remains stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle joint.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally inverted with the sole turned inward toward the body's midline, creating a pronounced angle at the ankle joint while the lower leg remains completely still and vertical. The resistance band is visibly taut and stretched, demonstrating full tension against the inward foot position. The tibialis anterior and other anterior tibial muscles appear contracted and defined along the front of the lower leg.

exercises.name: Heel-Toe Walking
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright and walking forward in a straight line by placing the heel of one foot directly in front of the toes of the other foot with each step, creating a tandem gait pattern. Arms may be extended to the sides for balance. The gaze is directed forward and the body remains tall and erect.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with one leg extended forward in a straight line, heel planted on the ground directly in front of the other foot's toes, while the back leg remains straight with the toe pushing off or just lifting. The torso is tall and vertical, core engaged, with arms extended laterally at shoulder height for balance, and the head faces forward with eyes focused ahead. The forward leg's hip flexors and anterior tibialis are visibly engaged, while the calf and posterior chain of the back leg show tension from the stabilization effort.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or wall for balance with one hand. The outside leg lifts straight out to the side away from the body to approximately 30 to 45 degrees while keeping the toes pointed forward and the knee straight. The standing leg remains stable and the torso does not lean to the opposite side.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright on the left leg. The right leg is lifted straight out to the side at approximately 45 degrees from the body. The right knee is straight and locked. Torso remains upright, not leaning.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or wall for balance. The inside leg crosses in front of the standing leg, sweeping inward across the body against resistance from a band or gravity. The torso remains upright and the pelvis stays level without tilting.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains straight and planted while the working leg is fully crossed in front of the body at approximately 45 degrees, with the knee slightly bent, creating a diagonal line across the midline of the torso. The torso stays completely upright and facing forward with shoulders level and pelvis square, while the inner thigh and adductor muscles are visibly contracted as the leg reaches its furthest inward position.

exercises.name: Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling lunge position with the right knee on the floor directly under the right hip, and the left foot flat on the floor in front with the left knee bent at 90 degrees. The torso is tall and upright, hips are pressed gently forward, and a deep stretch is felt in the front of the right hip and thigh. Hands rest on the front knee or at the waist.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a deep half-kneeling lunge with the right knee planted on the ground directly beneath the hip, while the left leg is positioned forward with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and foot flat. The torso remains tall and vertical, with the hips pressed forward in a tucked position, creating visible tension and engagement through the front of the right hip flexor and quadriceps. The person faces forward with hands either resting on the front knee or positioned at the waist, and the body appears symmetric from a lateral view.

exercises.name: Piriformis Stretch
exercises.pose_description: From a kneeling or seated position, one leg is crossed in front with the shin on the floor in a figure-four configuration. The torso leans forward over the crossed leg, bringing the chest toward the floor while keeping the hips squared. A deep stretch is felt in the outer hip and buttock of the front leg. Hands are placed on the floor in front for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is folded forward at approximately 45-90 degrees toward the floor, with the chest approaching or nearly touching the crossed front leg, while the back leg extends behind in a kneeling position with hips squared forward. The arms are extended in front with hands planted on the floor for support, the head is neutral or slightly lowered, and the glutes and outer hip muscles of the front leg appear visibly stretched and engaged. The person's weight is distributed between the hands and knees, creating a deep forward fold that emphasizes the posterior chain and hip external rotators.

exercises.name: IT Band Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with legs crossed, the back leg crossing behind the front leg. The body leans to the side of the front leg, pushing the hip of the back leg outward while reaching the arm overhead toward the opposite side. A stretch is felt along the outer thigh and hip of the back leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands with their right leg crossed behind their left leg, torso leaning distinctly to the left with the left arm stretched overhead and reaching diagonally across toward the right side, creating a pronounced lateral flexion curve from hip to fingertips. The right hip is pushed outward and back, the left knee maintains a slight bend, and the head follows the spinal curve while facing forward, with the outer right thigh and hip visibly lengthened.

exercises.name: Side-Lying Hip Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with the body in a straight line, bottom arm extended under the head for support. The top leg lifts straight upward toward the ceiling to approximately 30 to 45 degrees while keeping the knee straight and toes pointed forward. The hips remain stacked and do not roll forward or backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side in a straight line, with the top leg raised to approximately 45-60 degrees from the body, knee fully extended and toes pointed forward, while the bottom leg remains straight on the ground. The torso stays upright and stacked vertically above the bottom leg, with the bottom arm extended under the head and the top arm resting along the side of the torso. The abductor muscles on the outer hip and thigh of the top leg are visibly contracted and engaged, creating a defined line from hip to knee.

exercises.name: Fire Hydrants
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. One knee remains bent at 90 degrees and lifts out to the side, opening the hip like a fire hydrant, to approximately hip height. The spine stays neutral, the core is braced, and the pelvis does not rotate or shift.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in quadruped position with hands and knees planted firmly on the ground, while one leg is abducted outward with the knee bent at 90 degrees, lifted to approximately hip height and pointing perpendicular to the body. The lifted side's glute medius and hip abductor muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, the spine maintains a neutral line from head to hips, and the torso faces downward without any rotation or pelvic shift.

exercises.name: Monster Walks
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a quarter-squat position with a resistance band looped around the ankles or just above the knees. Feet are shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, and the torso is slightly hinged forward at the hips. Steps are taken diagonally forward and outward, maintaining tension on the band throughout, like a monster walking.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands with one leg extended diagonally forward and outward at approximately 45 degrees, knee slightly bent, while the opposite leg remains planted with a bent knee in a quarter-squat position, maintaining forward hip hinge. The resistance band is visibly taut between the legs, and the glutes, outer hip, and thigh muscles are prominently engaged and contracted on the extended leg side, with the torso remaining upright and stable.

exercises.name: Hip Circles
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with hands on hips and feet shoulder-width apart. The hips draw large, smooth circles in a clockwise or counterclockwise direction, rotating through flexion, lateral tilt, extension, and the opposite lateral tilt. The upper body remains as still as possible and the knees stay slightly soft.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with hands resting on hips, feet shoulder-width apart, and knees slightly bent. At the peak of the hip circle, the hips are maximally rotated to one side (either fully extended backward or tilted laterally), creating a visible asymmetrical line from shoulders through hips, while the upper body and head remain centered and still, facing forward. The oblique muscles on the extended side appear engaged and slightly lengthened, contrasting with the compressed appearance on the opposite side.

exercises.name: Seated Figure Four Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with good posture. One ankle is crossed over the opposite knee in a figure-four position, with the crossed knee dropping open to the side. The torso leans gently forward from the hips until a stretch is felt in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg. Hands may rest on the shin of the crossed leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright in a chair with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee, creating a 90-degree angle at the hip with the crossed knee dropped open laterally. The torso is folded forward from the hips at approximately 30-45 degrees, with the spine maintaining a gentle curve as hands rest on or near the shin of the crossed leg, while the glute and external rotator muscles of the crossed leg appear engaged and stretched. The head remains in neutral alignment with the spine, and the person faces forward or slightly downward.

exercises.name: Supine Hamstring Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one leg extended on the floor. The other leg is raised straight up toward the ceiling with the knee as straight as possible, hands clasped behind the thigh or a strap looped around the foot to assist the stretch. The hips remain flat on the floor and the lower back maintains a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with one leg fully extended along the floor and the other leg raised nearly perpendicular to the body (90+ degrees at the hip), knee straight or nearly straight, with hands clasped behind the thigh or a strap around the foot pulling gently toward the torso. The hamstring of the raised leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the hips remain square and flat against the floor, and the lower back maintains contact with the ground with the head neutral or slightly forward.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright on one leg, holding a wall or chair for balance with one hand. The opposite foot is grasped behind the body with the same-side hand, pulling the heel toward the buttock. Both knees remain close together, the pelvis is tucked slightly under, and the torso stays tall.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on one straight leg while the opposite leg is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled close to or touching the buttock, creating a vertical line from hip to knee. The same-side arm reaches back to grasp the foot/ankle, pulling it upward, while the supporting arm remains lightly on the wall or chair for balance. The torso is upright and squared forward, the pelvis is level and slightly tucked, and the quadriceps of the bent leg appear visibly stretched and engaged.

exercises.name: Mini Squats
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet shoulder-width apart. The hips push back and the knees bend to approximately 30 to 45 degrees in a partial squat, as if beginning to sit in a tall chair. Arms extend forward for counterbalance, the chest stays lifted, and the knees track over the toes without caving inward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures a person in a partial squat position with knees bent to approximately 30-45 degrees, hips pushed back, torso upright with chest lifted, and arms extended forward at shoulder height for balance. The quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles are visibly engaged and tensed, with the knees tracking directly over the toes and the back maintaining a neutral spine angle relative to the ground.

exercises.name: Terminal Knee Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing with a resistance band looped behind the knee, anchored to a fixed point behind the body. The knee starts in a slightly bent position, approximately 20 to 30 degrees of flexion. The leg presses forward and straightens fully against the band resistance, achieving complete knee extension. The standing leg and torso remain upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The working leg is fully extended straight ahead with the knee locked in complete extension (0 degrees of flexion), while the standing leg remains straight and stable supporting the upright torso. The quadriceps of the extended leg appear visibly contracted and engaged, with the resistance band stretched taut behind the knee. The person faces forward with shoulders square and neutral spine alignment.

exercises.name: Knee Flexion ROM
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the edge of a chair with the working foot on the floor. The heel slides backward under the chair, bending the knee as far as comfortably possible to increase range of motion. The opposite foot remains flat on the floor, and the hands may rest on the thighs or grip the chair seat for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright on the chair edge with the working knee bent to approximately 90-100 degrees or greater, with the heel positioned far back underneath the chair. The quadriceps and hip flexors appear engaged and shortened, while the hamstrings and calf muscles are visibly stretched. The torso stays vertical and stable, facing forward, with the non-working leg extended or relaxed.

exercises.name: Prone Knee Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms at sides or folded under the forehead. One knee bends, bringing the heel toward the buttock as far as comfortably possible. The hips remain pressed flat against the floor and the thigh of the bending leg does not lift off the surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down on the ground with their torso and hips flat against the floor, head turned to one side or resting on folded arms. One knee is deeply flexed with the heel drawn up toward the buttock at approximately 90 degrees or greater knee bend, while the opposite leg remains fully extended. The quadriceps of the bent leg and the hamstrings appear visibly engaged and contracted as the heel approaches the glute.

exercises.name: Lateral Step-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Standing beside a low step or platform with feet parallel. The foot closest to the step is placed on top of the step, and the body is driven upward by pressing through that foot until standing tall on the step. The movement is lateral rather than forward, and the arms may be held at the waist for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands fully upright on top of the step with their body weight centered over the stepping leg, which is straight and engaged. The opposite leg hangs naturally off the step with a slight bend at the knee, while the torso remains tall and perpendicular to the ground with shoulders level and stable. The quadriceps, glutes, and calf of the weight-bearing leg are visibly contracted and engaged.

exercises.name: Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, elbow pinned to the side of the body. A resistance band or cable is held in the hand. The forearm rotates inward across the body toward the stomach, working the internal rotators of the shoulder. The elbow stays firmly at the side throughout the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with the working arm bent at 90 degrees at the elbow, forearm rotated inward across the front of the body toward the midline/stomach, with the elbow remaining pinned against the ribcage. The shoulder internal rotators and anterior chest muscles appear visibly engaged and contracted, creating tension across the front shoulder and chest.

exercises.name: Shoulder Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms at sides, holding a light weight or no weight. One arm lifts straight forward and upward in front of the body with the elbow straight, palm facing down, reaching toward the ceiling in full shoulder flexion. The torso stays upright without arching the back, and the shoulder blade glides naturally along the ribcage.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm fully extended straight overhead at approximately 180 degrees of shoulder flexion, elbow locked straight, palm facing inward or forward, with the arm aligned vertically above the shoulder. The torso remains neutral and upright with no spinal arch, while the opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side, and the anterior deltoid, clavicular head of pectoralis major, and serratus anterior are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Shoulder Abduction
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms at sides. One arm lifts straight out to the side, away from the body, with the elbow straight and palm facing down, rising to shoulder height or above. The torso remains tall and does not lean to the opposite side, and the shoulder does not shrug upward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm extended fully straight out to the side at shoulder height (90-degree abduction), palm facing downward, while the opposite arm remains at their side. The torso is perfectly vertical with no lateral lean, the shoulder of the raised arm is packed down (not shrugged), and the deltoid and upper back muscles appear visibly engaged and contracted.

exercises.name: Sleeper Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on the involved side with the shoulder and elbow each bent to 90 degrees, forearm pointing toward the ceiling. The opposite hand gently pushes the forearm of the bottom arm downward toward the floor, internally rotating the shoulder. The elbow remains at shoulder height and the body stays on its side without rolling backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the involved shoulder's forearm pressed down toward the floor in deep internal rotation, creating approximately a 45-50 degree angle between the forearm and the ground, while the opposite hand applies gentle pressure on top of the forearm. The elbow remains at shoulder height, the torso stays flat and aligned on its side without rolling backward, and the posterior shoulder and rotator cuff muscles appear visibly stretched and engaged.

exercises.name: Cross-Body Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with one arm extended straight across the chest at shoulder height. The opposite hand cups the elbow or upper arm and gently pulls it closer to the body, creating a stretch across the posterior shoulder and upper back. The shoulders remain level and the torso does not twist.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm crossed horizontally across the chest at shoulder height, elbow bent approximately 90 degrees, while the opposite hand firmly grasps and pulls the crossed arm closer to the body, creating a visible compression across the posterior shoulder and upper back. The shoulders remain level and square, the spine stays neutral without rotation, and the stretched shoulder blade appears retracted as the chest and anterior shoulder muscles visibly lengthen on the pulling side.

exercises.name: Prone Y Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down or resting on the floor. Both arms lift upward and outward at approximately 45 degrees from the head, forming a Y shape, with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. The forehead rests on the floor, the shoulder blades squeeze together, and the arms lift to approximately ear height.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) on the floor with both arms extended upward and outward at approximately 45-degree angles from the body, forming a Y-shape with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling and arms at roughly ear height. The shoulder blades are visibly squeezed together, the upper back is engaged and slightly lifted, the forehead remains on the floor, and the core appears taut to maintain spinal stability.

exercises.name: Prone T Raises
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down or resting on the floor. Both arms lift straight out to the sides at 90 degrees from the torso, forming a T shape, with thumbs pointing toward the ceiling. The shoulder blades squeeze firmly together and the arms lift to body height. The forehead rests on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down with their body flat against the ground, arms extended directly out to the sides at 90 degrees from the torso in a perfect T-shape, with elbows straight and thumbs pointing upward toward the ceiling. The shoulder blades are pulled tightly together and the arms are lifted to approximately shoulder height, creating visible tension across the upper back and rear shoulders. The forehead remains resting on the floor while the chest and shoulders display prominent muscle engagement across the trapezius, rhomboids, and posterior deltoids.

exercises.name: Shoulder Shrugs
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms hanging at sides, holding light dumbbells or no weight. Both shoulders elevate straight upward toward the ears as high as possible, squeezing the upper trapezius at the top. The arms remain straight, the head stays neutral, and there is no head movement or neck rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with arms hanging straight down at their sides, shoulders elevated maximally toward the ears in a shrugged position, creating visible tension and bulging in the upper trapezius and neck region. The head remains in neutral position with no forward tilt or rotation, and the entire upper body appears rigid with the shrug contracted at its highest point.

exercises.name: Resistance Band Pull-Apart
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms extended straight in front at shoulder height, holding a resistance band with both hands about shoulder-width apart. The hands pull the band apart horizontally by squeezing the shoulder blades together, stretching the band across the chest until the arms are out to the sides. The elbows remain straight throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms extended straight out to the sides at shoulder height, forming a T-shape with the body, while holding a stretched resistance band with elbows locked in full extension. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear deltoids, with the chest lifted and shoulders drawn back.

exercises.name: Chin Tucks
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with the spine tall and shoulders relaxed. The chin draws straight backward, creating a double chin, as if pushing the back of the head against an imaginary wall. The eyes remain level, the head does not tilt up or down, and the movement is purely a horizontal retraction of the cervical spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: Standing upright facing forward. The chin is drawn fully backward and downward, creating a pronounced double chin. The head is retracted straight back, not tilted up or down. The neck is elongated at the back.

exercises.name: Neck Rotations
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with the spine tall and shoulders relaxed. The head turns slowly to one side, bringing the chin toward the shoulder, then returns to center and rotates to the opposite side. The shoulders remain still and level, and the movement is a smooth, controlled rotation of the cervical spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is rotated maximally to one side with the chin nearly touching or pointing toward the shoulder, while the torso remains perfectly still and upright facing forward. The neck muscles on the opposite side appear stretched and elongated, while the rotated side shows subtle engagement. The shoulders stay level and relaxed without any elevation or forward movement.

exercises.name: Neck Side Bends
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with the spine tall and shoulders relaxed. The head tilts to one side, bringing the ear toward the shoulder while the opposite shoulder remains depressed. One hand may gently assist the stretch by resting on top of the head. The face continues to point straight ahead without rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The head is maximally tilted toward one shoulder with the ear positioned as close as possible to the shoulder, while the opposite shoulder remains actively depressed and pulled downward, creating a visible stretch along the lateral neck and upper trapezius. The spine remains upright and tall with no rotation, the face points straight ahead, and one hand rests gently on top of the head applying light downward pressure, with the other arm relaxed at the side. The person maintains an upright standing posture with shoulders level relative to the hips, though the stretched side of the neck visibly lengthens.

exercises.name: Upper Trapezius Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright. One hand reaches behind the back or holds the seat of a chair to depress that shoulder. The head tilts toward the opposite side, bringing the ear toward the shoulder, and the free hand may gently rest on the head to add a mild overpressure. A stretch is felt along the side of the neck and upper trapezius.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their torso vertical and head tilted maximally toward one shoulder, bringing the ear close to that shoulder at approximately 45 degrees of lateral flexion. The opposite arm extends behind the back with the shoulder depressed downward, while the other hand rests gently on top of the head applying gentle overpressure. The upper trapezius on the stretched side appears elongated and taut along the neck-to-shoulder line.

exercises.name: Levator Scapulae Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright. The head rotates approximately 45 degrees to one side, then the chin tucks downward toward the armpit, looking diagonally down. The hand on the same side as the rotation gently assists by pulling the head further into the stretch. The opposite shoulder remains depressed, and a stretch is felt along the back of the neck on the opposite side.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their head rotated approximately 45 degrees to one side and chin tucked downward toward the same-side armpit, creating a diagonal downward gaze. The hand on the rotated side grasps or gently pulls the head, with the elbow bent and positioned near the chest, while the opposite shoulder is actively depressed downward. The posterior neck muscles on the non-rotated side appear visibly elongated and engaged in the stretch.

exercises.name: Prone Press-Up
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with hands positioned under the shoulders as if preparing for a push-up. The upper body presses upward by straightening the arms, lifting the chest off the floor while the hips and pelvis remain in contact with the floor. The lower back extends into a gentle arch, and the head looks forward. The arms may be fully or partially extended depending on comfort.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is viewed from the side, lying prone with arms fully or nearly fully extended, pressing the upper torso upward so the chest lifts several inches off the floor while the hips, pelvis, and thighs remain in contact with the ground. The lower back is noticeably arched, the head is held neutral or slightly extended looking forward, and the shoulders appear drawn back with visible engagement through the chest and anterior shoulders. The body forms a curved line from the extended arms through the arched spine to the grounded lower body.

exercises.name: Knee-to-Chest Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one knee pulled up toward the chest, both hands clasping below the kneecap or behind the thigh. The opposite leg remains extended flat on the floor. The lower back relaxes and rounds gently into the floor, and the head and shoulders remain on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and pulled maximally toward the chest, hands clasped firmly below the kneecap or around the back of the thigh, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and relaxed on the floor. The lower back is pressed into the floor with gentle rounding, the head and shoulders stay neutral on the ground, and the hamstrings and glutes of the bent-knee leg appear visibly engaged and stretched.

exercises.name: Double Knee-to-Chest
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees pulled up toward the chest simultaneously. Both hands wrap around the shins or behind the thighs, hugging the knees close. The lower back rounds gently into the floor, the tailbone lifts slightly, and the head and shoulders remain relaxed on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with both knees drawn maximally toward the chest, creating acute angles at the hips and knees (approximately 90 degrees each), while both hands clasp firmly around the shins or behind the thighs. The lower back is fully rounded and pressed into the floor with the tailbone lifted, the head remains neutral on the ground, and the abdominal and hip flexor muscles appear engaged and contracted as the body forms a compact, folded position.

exercises.name: Lumbar Rotation Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Both knees drop together to one side toward the floor while the shoulders and upper back remain flat on the ground. The arms are extended out to the sides in a T position for stability. The head may turn to look toward the opposite side of the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their torso flat against the ground while both knees are dropped maximally toward the floor on one side, creating a 45-60 degree angle at the hips. Their shoulders remain pressed flat on the ground perpendicular to their lower body, with arms extended outward in a T-position, and their head is turned to face the opposite direction of the dropped knees. The oblique and rotational muscles along the torso appear stretched and elongated across the twist created between the upper and lower body.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with arms extended straight toward the ceiling above the shoulders and both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees in a tabletop position. One arm reaches overhead toward the floor behind while the opposite leg extends straight out, lowering toward the floor without touching. The lower back remains pressed firmly into the ground throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one arm extended straight overhead toward the floor behind the head (shoulder flexed approximately 180 degrees) while the opposite leg extends fully straight, hovering just above the ground with the hip flexed at near 0 degrees; simultaneously, the other arm remains bent at 90 degrees with the hand reaching toward the ceiling and the opposite leg stays in the tabletop position with hip and knee both at 90 degrees. The lower back remains pressed flat against the ground, creating a diagonal line of tension across the torso from the extended arm to the extended leg, with visible abdominal and core musculature engaged to maintain spinal stability.

exercises.name: Plank
exercises.pose_description: Body supported on forearms and toes in a straight line from head to heels. Elbows directly under shoulders, forearms flat on floor, core tight, hips level — not sagging or piking.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfectly straight line from head to heels, held parallel to the ground with no sagging at the hips or pike at the shoulders. The forearms remain flat on the floor with elbows directly beneath the shoulders at 90-degree angles, while the core, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers appear visibly engaged and contracted. The person faces downward toward the floor with their neck neutral, shoulders packed down and back.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.pose_description: Body supported on one forearm and the side of the bottom foot, forming a straight line from head to feet. The supporting elbow is directly under the shoulder, the top arm rests on the hip or extends toward the ceiling. The hips are lifted high and do not sag toward the floor, and the core is fully engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfectly straight diagonal line from head to feet, balanced on the supporting forearm (elbow bent 90 degrees directly beneath the shoulder) and the outer edge of the bottom foot, with hips lifted high and aligned with shoulders and ankles. The top leg is fully extended and stacked directly over the bottom leg, while the top arm either rests along the torso or extends upward, with the entire lateral core, obliques, and shoulder stabilizers visibly contracted and tensioned. The head maintains neutral alignment with the spine, facing forward, with no sagging at the hips or rotation of the torso.

exercises.name: Abdominal Bracing
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. The abdominal muscles are contracted as if bracing for a punch to the stomach, creating a rigid cylinder around the midsection. The spine maintains its natural curve, the ribs do not flare, and breathing continues normally while the brace is held.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, while the abdominal wall appears deeply indented and rigidly contracted, creating a visible hollowed appearance across the entire midsection from sternum to pelvis. The torso maintains a neutral spine position with no arching or flaring of the ribs, and the rectus abdominis, transverse abdominis, and obliques all appear maximally engaged and tensioned like a tight corset around the core.

exercises.name: Supine Marching
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. One knee lifts toward the chest to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion while the opposite foot remains on the floor. The legs alternate in a slow marching motion, and the lower back stays pressed against the floor with the core engaged throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with one knee lifted toward the chest at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion while the opposite leg remains extended with the foot flat on the floor; the lower back is pressed firmly against the floor and the abdominal muscles appear visibly engaged and contracted. The lifted knee is directly above the hip joint, the arms rest at the sides or across the chest for stability, and the head remains neutral against the floor.

exercises.name: Seated Spinal Twist
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with one leg extended straight and the other leg crossed over with the foot flat on the floor outside the opposite knee. The torso rotates toward the bent knee, and the opposite elbow hooks outside the bent knee for leverage. The sitting bones remain grounded, the spine stays tall, and the rotation comes from the thoracic and lumbar spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is rotated maximally toward the bent knee, with the spine twisted from the thoracic spine, while the head follows the rotation to gaze over the shoulder. The hooked elbow presses against the outside of the bent knee for leverage, the extended leg remains straight on the floor, the opposite arm reaches behind for balance or wraps around the torso, and the sitting bones stay planted as the obliques and spinal rotators appear fully engaged and lengthened on the extended side.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position. One arm threads underneath the body, reaching through the space between the opposite arm and knee, with the shoulder and temple resting on the floor. The hips remain over the knees, and the supporting arm may stay straight or bend slightly. A deep rotation stretch is felt through the thoracic spine and shoulder.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is in a deep spinal rotation with the right shoulder and right temple pressed flat against the floor, the right arm fully threaded underneath the torso with the palm facing up, while the left arm remains straight and supporting the upper body weight. The hips stay squared over the knees in a kneeling position, and the head is turned to face downward toward the floor with the spine twisted maximally through the thoracic region, creating visible tension through the shoulder blade, obliques, and upper back muscles.

exercises.name: Thoracic Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright or seated in a chair with hands clasped behind the head. The upper back gently arches backward, extending through the thoracic spine while the lumbar spine stays relatively neutral. The elbows pull back and the chest lifts toward the ceiling, opening the front of the body. The movement is controlled and focused on the mid-back region.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their upper back maximally extended backward, chest lifted and opened toward the ceiling, while their hands remain clasped behind their head with elbows pulled back and wide. The thoracic spine displays a pronounced backward curve while the lower back stays neutral, creating visible engagement across the mid-back, rear shoulders, and chest muscles that appear stretched and extended.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with one arm extended straight in front at shoulder height, palm facing up. The opposite hand grasps the fingers and gently pulls them downward and back toward the body, extending the wrist. A stretch is felt along the inner forearm and wrist flexor muscles. The elbow of the stretching arm remains straight.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their stretching arm extended straight ahead at shoulder height, palm facing downward with wrist fully extended backward. Their opposite hand firmly grasps their fingers and pulls them toward their body, creating a pronounced backward bend at the wrist while the elbow remains locked and straight. The inner forearm and wrist flexor muscles appear visibly taut and elongated.

exercises.name: Wrist Extensor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with one arm extended straight in front at shoulder height, palm facing down. The opposite hand grasps the back of the hand and gently pulls it downward, flexing the wrist. A stretch is felt along the outer forearm and wrist extensor muscles. The elbow of the stretching arm remains straight.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their right arm extended straight ahead at shoulder height, palm facing downward, while their left hand pulls the right hand downward with the wrist fully flexed (fingers pointing toward the ground). The right elbow remains locked in full extension, and the forearm extensors along the outer forearm are visibly tensioned and engaged as the wrist reaches maximum downward bend.

exercises.name: Grip Strengthening
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with the arm at the side or supported on a surface. The hand squeezes a grip strengthener, stress ball, or tennis ball, closing all fingers firmly around the object with maximum contraction. The wrist remains in a neutral position, and the forearm muscles visibly contract during the squeeze.
exercises.end_pose_description: The hand is fully closed into a tight fist around the grip strengthener, with all fingers curled inward at maximum contraction and the thumb pressing against the fingers. The forearm is prominently flexed with visible muscle definition in the flexor digitorum and flexor carpi radialis, while the wrist remains neutral and straight, and the arm stays relaxed at the side or on the support surface with the elbow at approximately 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Finger Tendon Glides
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with one hand extended in front, palm facing away. The fingers move through a series of positions: straight extension, hook fist (tips bent to pads), full fist, straight fist (fingers curled at knuckles only), and tabletop (fingers bent at knuckles to 90 degrees with fingertips pointing forward). Each position is held briefly before transitioning.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one arm extended at shoulder height, palm facing away, fingers curled into a tabletop position where the metacarpophalangeal joints are bent at approximately 90 degrees while the fingertips point directly forward and the hand appears flat across the top. The forearm remains straight and parallel to the ground, with visible tension in the finger extensors and intrinsic hand muscles creating definition across the back of the hand and fingers.

exercises.name: Wrist Circles
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated with the forearm supported or the arm extended in front. The hand draws slow circles in the air by rotating at the wrist joint, moving through flexion, radial deviation, extension, and ulnar deviation in a smooth continuous motion. The forearm remains still and the movement is isolated to the wrist.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures the arm extended forward at shoulder height with the wrist fully extended backward (dorsiflexion), creating a 90-degree angle between the forearm and hand, while the forearm remains rigid and still. The person faces forward with shoulders relaxed and stable, and the wrist extensors on the top of the forearm appear visibly engaged as the hand completes the upward arc of the circular motion.

exercises.name: Tennis Ball Roll
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with one foot resting on a tennis ball placed on the floor. Gentle downward pressure is applied through the foot as it rolls the ball from the toes to the heel and across the arch, massaging the plantar fascia. The opposite foot remains flat on the floor, and the body weight shifts slightly to increase or decrease pressure.
exercises.end_pose_description: The seated figure has their working foot rolled back toward the heel with the tennis ball positioned under the arch, knee bent at approximately 90 degrees while the opposite leg remains extended with foot flat on the floor. The torso remains upright and centered in the chair, with visible engagement through the calf and foot musculature as body weight presses downward through the rolling foot, creating tension across the plantar fascia and arch area.

exercises.name: Toe Raises
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or chair for balance. The toes and forefoot lift off the ground while the heels remain planted, dorsiflexing the ankles and engaging the tibialis anterior. The body weight shifts slightly back onto the heels, and the torso stays upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with heels firmly planted on the ground and toes/forefoot lifted as high as possible, creating a pronounced dorsiflexion angle at the ankles (approximately 45-60 degrees). The shins appear visibly tense with the tibialis anterior muscles clearly engaged and defined, while the calves are stretched and elongated. The torso remains perfectly vertical and stable, with the person's weight noticeably shifted back onto their heels.

exercises.name: Marble Pickup
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with one foot bare and marbles or small objects scattered on the floor. The toes grip and pick up individual marbles, transferring them to a cup or different location. The heel remains on the floor, and the foot flexors work to curl the toes around each marble.
exercises.end_pose_description: The seated person's bare foot is lifted slightly off the floor with toes fully curled and flexed around a marble, holding it suspended above the ground before depositing it into the cup. The calf and foot muscles are visibly contracted and engaged, with the toes forming a tight grip, while the heel remains anchored to the floor and the knee maintains a slight bend at approximately 90 degrees. The person faces forward in an upright seated posture with their torso stable against the chair back.

exercises.name: Calf Stretch on Step
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the edge of a step with the balls of the feet on the step and the heels hanging off the back edge. One or both heels drop below the level of the step, creating a deep stretch in the calf muscles. Hands hold a railing or wall for balance, and the knees are straight to target the gastrocnemius.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright on a step with knees fully extended and straight, while both heels are dropped significantly below the step level, creating a pronounced downward angle at the ankles. The calf muscles appear visibly stretched and taut, with the body weight distributed through the balls of the feet on the step edge. Hands grip a railing or wall for stability, and the torso remains vertical and facing forward.

exercises.name: Soleus Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing facing a wall with hands placed on the wall at shoulder height. One foot is positioned behind the other in a staggered stance. The back knee bends while keeping the heel on the floor, creating a stretch in the lower calf (soleus) of the back leg. The front knee is also slightly bent and the torso leans slightly forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in a deep forward lean against the wall with both hands pressed firmly at shoulder height, the back leg's knee deeply flexed (approximately 60-90 degrees) while the heel remains planted on the ground, and the front leg's knee bent at roughly 45 degrees to support the forward weight shift. The torso is angled forward noticeably from the hips, the soleus muscle of the back calf is visibly taut and stretched, and the person faces directly toward the wall with their body perpendicular to the ground.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raises
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. The heels lift off the ground as high as possible, pushing up onto the balls of the feet while the toes remain on the floor. Additional weight may be placed on the knees for resistance. The movement is controlled up and down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Seated on a chair with feet on the ground. Both heels are lifted high off the ground, rising up onto the balls of the feet. The calf muscles are visibly contracted. Knees are bent at 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Wall Push-Ups
exercises.pose_description: Standing approximately arm's length from a wall with hands placed flat on the wall at shoulder height and shoulder-width apart. The body leans forward toward the wall by bending the elbows, then pushes back to the starting position. The body maintains a straight line from head to heels, with the core engaged and heels slightly lifted.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person's arms are fully extended, pushing the body away from the wall to return to the starting position, with elbows locked straight and shoulders packed back. The body forms a rigid plank line from head to heels, angled slightly away from the wall at approximately 10-15 degrees, with the core visibly engaged and heels still slightly lifted off the ground. The chest appears expanded and the shoulders are retracted, showing activation through the pectorals, shoulders, and triceps.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing next to a wall or doorframe with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and pinned against the side. The back of the wrist or hand presses outward into the wall or doorframe with sustained effort, as if trying to externally rotate the shoulder. No visible movement occurs — the contraction is purely isometric. The torso remains upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing perpendicular to the wall, with their right elbow bent at 90 degrees and pressed firmly against their ribcage, while their wrist and forearm are pressed outward against the wall in external rotation—the shoulder and rotator cuff muscles visibly tensed and engaged. The torso remains perfectly still and aligned vertically, with the opposite arm at rest, and the face looks straight ahead as sustained isometric tension is held through the shoulder external rotators.

exercises.name: Isometric Shoulder Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Standing next to a wall or doorframe with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and pinned against the side. The palm or front of the wrist presses inward into the wall or doorframe with sustained effort, as if trying to internally rotate the shoulder. No visible movement occurs — the contraction is purely isometric. The torso remains upright.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing perpendicular to the wall, with their right elbow bent at 90 degrees and pressed firmly against their ribcage, while their forearm and palm are pressed inward against the wall with maximum isometric tension. The shoulder and chest muscles on the working side appear visibly contracted and engaged, with the torso remaining stable and squared, demonstrating sustained internal rotation force against the immovable surface.

exercises.name: Bicep Curls
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with a dumbbell or resistance band in each hand, arms at sides with palms facing forward. The forearms curl upward by bending the elbows, bringing the weights toward the shoulders while keeping the elbows pinned at the sides. The torso remains still without swaying, and the upper arms do not move.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, dumbbells held at shoulder height with palms facing forward. The upper arms remain stationary and close to the torso, while the forearms are vertical or slightly angled back toward the shoulders. The biceps appear fully contracted and engaged, creating visible muscle definition in the upper arms.

exercises.name: Tricep Extensions
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a dumbbell or resistance band overhead with both hands or one hand. The elbow points toward the ceiling and the forearm lowers behind the head by bending at the elbow, then extends back to full lockout overhead. The upper arm remains stationary next to the ear, and the core is braced.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with the dumbbell or resistance band fully extended overhead, arm(s) straight with elbows locked out and aligned vertically alongside the ears. The triceps appear fully contracted and engaged, with visible definition along the back of the upper arm, while the core remains braced and the torso stable.

exercises.name: Wrist Curls
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with the forearm resting on a table or thigh, palm facing up, holding a light dumbbell. The wrist curls upward, lifting the weight by flexing the wrist while the forearm remains stationary. The fingers may open slightly at the bottom and close at the top to increase range of motion.
exercises.end_pose_description: The forearm remains flat and stationary on the table or thigh while the wrist is fully flexed upward at approximately 70-80 degrees, with the dumbbell lifted toward the ceiling and the palm still facing up. The fingers are slightly spread open, and the flexor muscles of the forearm appear prominently contracted and defined. The upper body remains upright and still, with only the wrist joint showing active movement.

exercises.name: Reverse Wrist Curls
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with the forearm resting on a table or thigh, palm facing down, holding a light dumbbell. The wrist extends upward, lifting the back of the hand toward the ceiling while the forearm remains stationary. The movement is small and controlled, targeting the wrist extensors.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated with their forearm flat and stable on a table or thigh, palm facing downward, while the hand is fully extended upward at the wrist with fingers pointing toward the ceiling—the wrist is at maximum extension. The forearm remains completely still and neutral, highlighting the engaged wrist extensor muscles on the top of the forearm, while the dumbbell is held at the highest point of the movement with the back of the hand elevated.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Thoracic Extension
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back with a foam roller positioned horizontally under the mid-back at the level of the shoulder blades. Knees are bent with feet flat on the floor, and hands are clasped behind the head to support the neck. The upper back gently arches over the roller, extending the thoracic spine while the hips remain on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their back with the foam roller positioned under the mid-back, their chest prominently arched backward in maximum thoracic extension while hips remain planted on the floor and knees stay bent with feet flat. The hands remain clasped behind the head with elbows spread wide, and the head gently extends back without straining the neck, creating a pronounced C-curve through the upper spine that stretches the chest and anterior shoulders. The abdominal and hip flexor muscles appear lengthened while the upper back musculature is visibly engaged around the roller.

exercises.name: Foam Roller IT Band
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with a foam roller positioned under the outer thigh between the hip and the knee. The bottom leg is extended straight, and the top leg may cross over in front with the foot flat on the floor for support and pressure control. The hands and forearms support the upper body off the ground as the body rolls slowly up and down the roller along the IT band.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is positioned on their side with the foam roller pressed firmly into the upper outer thigh/hip area, body weight supported through forearms and hands on the ground. The bottom leg is fully extended straight along the ground, while the top leg is crossed over with knee bent and foot planted in front of the body for stability, creating a stacked side-lying position. The IT band, glute medius, and hip stabilizer muscles appear engaged and compressed against the roller.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Quad
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down in a modified plank position with a foam roller positioned under the front of both thighs. The forearms support the upper body, and the toes may be off the ground. The body rolls slowly forward and backward, moving the roller from just above the kneecaps to the hip flexors, applying pressure to the quadriceps.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a prone plank position with forearms flat on the ground, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, and the foam roller positioned at the highest point on the thighs near the hip flexors. The body is nearly horizontal and parallel to the ground with core muscles visibly engaged, legs extended straight behind with toes lightly touching or hovering, and the quadriceps appear compressed and engaged against the roller as the upper body weight presses down through the forearms.

exercises.name: Foam Roller Calf
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with legs extended and a foam roller positioned under both calves. Hands are placed behind the hips on the floor, lifting the buttocks slightly off the ground. The body rolls forward and backward, moving the roller from just above the ankles to below the knees, applying pressure along the calf muscles.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated on the floor with their torso leaning slightly backward, arms extended behind them with hands pressing into the floor to support lifted hips, while both legs are extended and the foam roller is positioned at the furthest point of the roll (either fully toward the ankles or fully toward the knees, depending on direction). The calf muscles appear maximally engaged and compressed against the foam roller, with the body weight distributed between the hands and the roller contact point.

exercises.name: Seated Row with Band
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with legs extended straight in front and a resistance band looped around the feet. Both hands grip the band with palms facing each other. The elbows pull straight back, squeezing the shoulder blades together, drawing the hands toward the lower ribs. The torso remains upright and does not lean backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated upright with legs extended straight, elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees and pulled tightly against the ribcage, with hands drawn back toward the lower chest/ribs while maintaining a neutral spine. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, the chest is slightly puffed forward, and the back musculature (lats and rhomboids) appears maximally contracted and engaged. The resistance band remains taut between the looped feet and the hands at the end position.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown with Band
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair or on the floor with a resistance band anchored overhead. Both hands grip the band wider than shoulder-width with palms facing forward. The elbows pull downward and back, driving the band toward the upper chest while squeezing the shoulder blades together. The torso remains upright and the core stays engaged.
