exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated upright with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, positioned close to the ribcage with upper arms nearly vertical and forearms angled slightly forward. The resistance band is pulled down to upper chest level with both hands roughly shoulder-width apart, shoulder blades visibly retracted and depressed, creating prominent definition across the lats, rhomboids, and upper back. The torso remains perpendicular to the ground with chest slightly lifted, facing directly forward.

exercises.name: Standing Row with Band
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with a resistance band anchored in front at chest height. Both hands grip the band with arms extended forward. The elbows pull straight back past the torso, squeezing the shoulder blades together and drawing the hands toward the lower ribs. The feet are staggered for stability and the torso stays tall.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with elbows bent at approximately 90 degrees, pulled tight against the ribcage with hands drawn back toward the lower chest/upper abdomen. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear shoulders, while the chest is slightly puffed forward. The resistance band is maximally stretched with tension visible in the biceps and upper back musculature.

exercises.name: Resisted Ankle Dorsiflexion
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with a resistance band looped around the top of the forefoot, anchored to a fixed point in front. The foot pulls upward against the band resistance, dorsiflexing the ankle and bringing the toes toward the shin. The heel remains on the floor and the lower leg stays stationary.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally dorsiflexed with toes pulled sharply toward the shin at approximately 20-30 degrees upward from neutral, while the heel remains planted on the floor and the lower leg stays vertical and stationary. The anterior tibialis muscle on the front of the shin appears visibly engaged and contracted, creating visible definition along the front of the lower leg. The resistance band is at maximum stretch tension across the top of the forefoot.

exercises.name: Resisted Ankle Plantarflexion
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with a resistance band looped around the ball of the foot, anchored behind the body or held in the hands. The foot pushes downward against the band resistance, plantarflexing the ankle and pointing the toes. The lower leg stays stationary and the movement occurs purely at the ankle.
exercises.end_pose_description: The foot is maximally plantarflexed with toes pointed downward at approximately 45-60 degrees below the horizontal plane, while the lower leg remains completely stationary and vertical. The calf muscle is visibly contracted and tightened, the resistance band is stretched taut beneath the ball of the foot, and the upper body remains upright and stable with no compensatory movement.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin or at sides. One leg lifts straight off the floor behind the body, squeezing the glute to drive the movement, while the knee remains straight. The hips and pelvis stay pressed into the floor, and the leg lifts to approximately 15 to 20 degrees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone (face down) with their torso and head still pressed into the floor, while one leg is extended straight behind them at approximately 15-20 degrees of hip extension, creating a visible lift from the glute contraction. The extended leg maintains a straight knee with the foot pointed slightly downward, while the opposite leg remains flat on the floor and the pelvis stays firmly grounded. The glute of the working leg appears visibly contracted and engaged at the peak of the lift.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both legs extended. One knee bends and lifts toward the chest, driven by the hip flexors, bringing the thigh to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion. The opposite leg remains flat on the floor, the lower back stays neutral, and the hands may gently guide the knee.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with one knee bent and drawn up toward the chest at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and flat on the floor. The hip flexors and iliopsoas are visibly engaged as the bent knee approaches the torso, the lower back maintains contact with the floor, and the hands gently cradle the lifted knee. The head and shoulders remain relaxed against the ground, facing upward.

exercises.name: Seated Knee Extension
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. One leg extends straight out in front by straightening the knee until the leg is parallel with the floor, engaging the quadriceps. The thigh remains on the seat, the back stays against the chair, and the movement is controlled both up and down.
exercises.end_pose_description: Seated on a chair or bench. The right leg is extended fully forward, straight and parallel to the floor. The knee is locked. The quadriceps muscle is visibly engaged. The left foot remains flat on the ground.

exercises.name: Hamstring Stretch with Strap
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one leg extended on the floor. A strap, towel, or belt is looped around the foot of the other leg, which is raised straight up toward the ceiling with the knee as straight as possible. Both hands hold the ends of the strap and gently pull the leg closer, deepening the hamstring stretch. The hips remain flat on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with their lower back and hips pressed firmly into the floor. One leg remains extended straight on the ground while the other leg is pulled nearly vertical toward the chest, with the knee nearly straight and the foot dorsiflexed, as both hands grip the strap around the foot and draw it slightly past vertical toward the torso. The hamstring, calf, and posterior chain of the elevated leg appear fully engaged and stretched, while the torso remains flat and stable against the ground.

exercises.name: Wall Angel
exercises.pose_description: Standing with the back, head, and buttocks flat against a wall. Arms are raised with the backs of the hands, wrists, and elbows pressed against the wall in a goalpost position. The arms slide upward along the wall toward full overhead extension and back down, maintaining constant contact between the arms and the wall throughout the arc of movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright against the wall with arms fully extended overhead in a straight vertical line, palms facing forward and the backs of the hands, wrists, and inner arms maintained in contact with the wall surface. The shoulders appear engaged and drawn upward, the core is visibly braced, and the entire posterior chain from heels through head remains flush against the wall, creating a continuous straight line from feet to fingertips.

exercises.name: Chest Stretch Corner
exercises.pose_description: Standing facing a corner of a room with one foot slightly forward. Both forearms are placed on the adjoining walls at approximately shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees. The body leans into the corner until a stretch is felt across the chest and front of the shoulders. The core is engaged and the lower back does not arch excessively.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person faces directly into the corner with their torso upright and squared toward the walls, both forearms pressed flat against the adjoining walls at shoulder height with elbows bent at 90 degrees, creating a symmetrical frame. The chest is visibly expanded and drawn forward into the corner, with the pectoral muscles and front deltoids appearing stretched and engaged, while the core remains braced with a neutral spine.

exercises.name: Isometric Quad Contraction
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with a small rolled towel or bolster placed under one knee. The knee presses downward into the towel, tightening the quadriceps and lifting the heel slightly off the floor. The contraction is held isometrically, the ankle is dorsiflexed, and the opposite leg rests extended on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with the working leg's knee bent approximately 20-30 degrees, pressing firmly down into the towel beneath it while the heel lifts visibly off the floor; the foot is dorsifexed with toes pointing toward the shin, and the quadriceps muscle of the working leg appears visibly contracted and tightened. The opposite leg remains fully extended and relaxed on the floor, while the torso stays flat against the ground facing upward.

exercises.name: Heel Drops
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the edge of a step with the balls of the feet on the step, heels hanging off the back. Starting from a raised calf raise position on both feet, the weight shifts to one foot and the heel slowly lowers below the level of the step in a controlled eccentric motion. Hands hold a railing for balance.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands on a step in profile, with one leg supporting their weight while the opposite heel is lowered well below the step level, creating a deep dorsiflexion stretch through the calf. The supporting leg is nearly straight with minimal knee bend, the torso remains upright and stable, and the hand grips the railing for balance as the lowered calf muscle appears fully lengthened and engaged. The person faces forward with shoulders square to the direction of travel.

exercises.name: Eccentric Calf Lowering
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the edge of a step with the balls of both feet on the step. Starting from a full calf raise on both feet, the weight transfers to one leg, and that heel slowly lowers below the step level over three to five seconds. The knee remains straight, and the opposite foot assists for the return to the top position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands on a step with one leg straight and that heel dropped significantly below step level, creating a deep calf stretch with the foot dorsiflexed (toes pointing upward), while the opposite leg is bent with foot lifted off the step to assist with balance. The torso remains upright and perpendicular to the ground, with engaged calf muscles visibly stretched on the lowered leg and the standing leg's calf fully lengthened.

exercises.name: Supine Piriformis Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. One ankle crosses over the opposite knee in a figure-four position. Both hands reach through the gap and clasp behind the thigh of the bottom leg, pulling it toward the chest. A deep stretch is felt in the outer hip and glute of the crossed leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with the bottom leg pulled toward the chest at approximately 90 degrees at the hip, while the top leg's ankle remains crossed over the bottom knee in a figure-four position with the hip externally rotated. The glutes and outer hip of the crossed leg appear fully engaged and stretched, with visible tension in the piriformis. Both shoulders remain flat on the ground, and the head stays neutral or slightly tilted to either side.

exercises.name: Seated Long Sitting Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with both legs extended straight in front, feet together and toes pointing up. The torso hinges forward from the hips, reaching both hands toward the toes while keeping the back as flat as possible. The knees remain pressed into the floor, and the stretch is felt along the hamstrings and lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is folded forward at the hips with the head positioned near or toward the shins, arms extended straight alongside or grasping the legs/feet, and the back forms a continuous rounded curve from the shoulders to the lower back. Both legs remain fully extended and pressed flat against the floor with knees locked straight, feet flexed with toes pointing upward, creating maximum length through the posterior chain from the hamstrings to the upper back.

exercises.name: Sciatic Nerve Glide
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one hip and knee bent to 90 degrees, hands clasping behind the thigh. The knee slowly straightens, extending the foot toward the ceiling while the ankle alternates between dorsiflexion and plantarflexion to glide the sciatic nerve. The opposite leg remains flat on the floor, and the movement is smooth and pain-free.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with the working leg extended nearly straight toward the ceiling (knee at approximately 10-20 degrees of flexion), foot positioned with the ankle in dorsiflexion (toes pointing toward the face), while the clasped hands remain behind the thigh providing gentle support. The non-working leg remains flat and relaxed on the floor, and the person's torso and head stay neutral against the ground with minimal movement.

exercises.name: Median Nerve Glide
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the affected arm extended out to the side at shoulder height. Starting with the wrist flexed and fingers curled toward the palm, the wrist gradually extends and the fingers straighten while the head tilts away from the outstretched arm. The movement alternates fluidly between the tensioned and relaxed positions to glide the median nerve.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with the affected arm extended fully straight out to the side at shoulder height, wrist fully extended backward and fingers spread open and straightened. The head is tilted away from the outstretched arm, creating a visible diagonal line of tension from the fingertips through the torso. The chest faces forward while the extended arm remains perpendicular to the body, with visible engagement through the forearm and shoulder stabilizers.

exercises.name: Ulnar Nerve Glide
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the affected arm at the side. The elbow bends to bring the hand toward the shoulder with the wrist extended and fingers pointing outward, then the arm extends outward to the side while the wrist curls and the head tilts away. The movement alternates smoothly between bent and extended positions to glide the ulnar nerve along its path.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with the affected arm fully extended out to the side at shoulder height, the elbow straight, wrist flexed downward with fingers curling toward the palm, and the head tilted away from the extended arm. The opposite side of the torso shows slight elongation from the lateral flexion, while the extended arm's forearm muscles appear engaged from the wrist flexion position.

exercises.name: Prone Shoulder Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with the forehead resting on the floor and arms extended overhead on the ground. One or both arms lift straight off the floor with thumbs pointing up, raising the arm as high as possible while keeping the forehead down and the rest of the body flat. The shoulder blade retracts and depresses as the arm lifts.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) with forehead remaining on the floor, one or both arms raised straight overhead at approximately 180 degrees of shoulder flexion, with thumbs pointing upward and arms fully extended. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and depressed, creating prominent muscle definition across the upper back, rear shoulders, and lower trapezius, while the torso and lower body remain flat and stationary against the ground.

exercises.name: Side-Lying External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lying on the uninvolved side with the working arm on top. The elbow of the top arm is bent to 90 degrees and pinned against the side with a small towel roll between the elbow and the ribcage. A light dumbbell is held in the hand, and the forearm rotates upward toward the ceiling, externally rotating the shoulder. The elbow remains stationary throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the working arm's elbow still bent at 90 degrees and anchored against the ribcage, while the forearm is rotated upward so the dumbbell points toward the ceiling, creating a vertical line from elbow to hand. The shoulder is externally rotated maximally, with the posterior shoulder and rotator cuff muscles visibly engaged and contracted. The torso remains stable and flat against the ground, perpendicular to the floor.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a wall or chair for balance. One knee lifts forward and upward in front of the body, bringing the thigh toward the chest until the hip reaches approximately 90 degrees of flexion. The knee is bent, the standing leg remains straight, and the torso stays tall without leaning backward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing figure faces forward with the torso upright and vertical, one leg extended straight down to support the body while the other knee is raised high in front, with the thigh parallel to the ground at approximately 90 degrees hip flexion and the knee bent at roughly 90 degrees. The lifted leg's hip flexors and quadriceps appear visibly engaged, the standing leg's quadriceps and glutes are tensed to maintain stability, and the core appears braced to keep the torso from leaning backward.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a wall or chair for balance. One leg extends straight behind the body, squeezing the glute to drive the movement, while the knee remains straight. The torso stays upright and does not lean forward excessively. The leg lifts to approximately 15 to 20 degrees of hip extension.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with one leg extended straight behind the body at approximately 45 degrees of hip extension, knee fully straight, while the supporting leg remains vertical and locked. The torso remains perpendicular to the ground with no forward lean, and the glute of the extended leg appears visibly contracted and engaged. The arms maintain contact with the wall or chair for balance.

exercises.name: Seated Ankle Pumps
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair or on a bed with legs extended in front or feet hanging off the edge. The ankles alternately pump up and down, dorsiflexing to pull the toes toward the shins, then plantarflexing to point the toes away. The movement is rhythmic and continuous, promoting circulation and ankle mobility.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright in the chair with one foot plantarflexed (toes pointed away from the body, heel anchored) while the other foot is dorsiflexed (toes pulled up toward the shin). The calf muscles of the plantarflexed leg appear engaged and tightened, while the shin muscles of the dorsiflexed leg show tension. The torso remains stable and upright against the chair back, with arms resting naturally.

exercises.name: Short Arc Quads
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with a bolster or rolled towel placed under one knee, supporting it in approximately 20 to 30 degrees of flexion. The lower leg straightens fully by extending the knee, lifting the foot off the floor while the thigh stays on the bolster. The quadriceps contract to lock the knee straight, and the ankle is dorsiflexed.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine on their back with one knee fully extended and locked straight, the foot lifted several inches off the floor with the toes pointing upward (dorsiflexed ankle), while the thigh remains supported on the bolster beneath it. The quadriceps muscle on the extended leg appears visibly contracted and taut from hip to knee, creating a defined line along the front of the thigh. The opposite leg remains relaxed on the floor, and the torso stays flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Long Arc Quads
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back or seated on the edge of a high surface with the knee bent at 90 degrees. The lower leg extends fully by straightening the knee through the complete range of motion until the leg is horizontal. The quadriceps work through the full arc from bent to straight, and the movement is controlled in both directions.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains supine or seated with their torso stable and upright, while the exercised leg is fully extended and horizontal to the ground with the knee completely straight (0 degrees flexion). The quadriceps muscles are visibly contracted and taut along the front of the thigh, creating a defined ridge from hip to knee, while the opposite leg remains in the starting position with knee bent at 90 degrees.

exercises.name: Supine Hip Internal Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor wider than hip-width apart. One knee drops inward toward the midline while the foot stays planted, internally rotating the hip. The opposite leg remains still, the pelvis stays level, and the movement is controlled through the available range of internal rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their right knee dropped maximally inward toward the left side of their body, creating an acute angle at the hip while the right foot remains planted on the floor, and the left leg stays stationary with knee bent at approximately 90 degrees. The pelvis remains level against the floor, the torso stays flat and centered, and the internal rotators of the right hip appear engaged and stretched as the knee points toward the midline.

exercises.name: Supine Hip External Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with both knees bent and feet flat on the floor. One knee drops outward away from the midline while the foot stays planted, externally rotating the hip. The opposite leg remains still, the pelvis stays level, and the movement is controlled through the available range of external rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies flat on their back with the left knee bent approximately 90 degrees and dropped maximally outward toward the floor, with the left foot remaining planted and the lower leg externally rotated, while the right leg stays stationary with knee bent and foot flat. The pelvis remains level and neutral, the torso stays flat against the ground, and the glutes and hip external rotators of the working leg appear engaged and stretched at end-range.

exercises.name: BOSU Ball Balance
exercises.pose_description: Standing on the dome side of a BOSU ball with feet hip-width apart or on a single leg. The knees are slightly bent, the core is engaged, and the arms are at sides or extended for balance. The body works to maintain equilibrium on the unstable surface while keeping the torso upright and the gaze directed forward at a fixed point.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall and stationary on the dome side of the BOSU ball with feet hip-width apart (or balanced on a single leg), knees slightly bent to maintain stability, torso upright and aligned over the base of support, core visibly engaged through a neutral spine, and arms either extended outward at shoulder height or positioned for counterbalance. The gaze is fixed forward at a focal point, with visible muscle engagement through the legs (quadriceps and glutes), core, and stabilizer muscles working to resist any wobbling on the unstable surface.

exercises.name: Single Leg Deadlift
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with a slight bend in the standing knee. The torso hinges forward at the hips while the non-standing leg extends straight behind, creating a T shape with the body. The arms hang down or hold a weight, the back remains flat, and the hips stay squared to the floor. The movement is a controlled hip hinge with the hamstrings and glutes of the standing leg working eccentrically.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is nearly parallel to the ground in a deep hip hinge, with the standing leg's knee slightly bent and the non-standing leg extended straight back at hip height, forming a perfect horizontal line from the back leg through the torso. The back remains flat and rigid, the arms hang vertically downward (or hold a weight at the hips), and the standing leg's hamstrings and glutes appear fully engaged and tensioned. The person faces downward with their gaze following the neutral spine alignment.

exercises.name: Bulgarian Split Squat
exercises.pose_description: Standing about two feet in front of a bench or elevated surface with the top of one foot resting on the bench behind. The front foot is flat on the floor. The body lowers by bending the front knee to approximately 90 degrees while the back knee drops toward the floor. The torso stays upright, and the front knee tracks over the toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: The front leg is bent to approximately 90 degrees at the knee with the thigh nearly parallel to the ground, while the back knee hovers just above the floor in a deep lunge position. The torso remains upright and vertical, perpendicular to the ground, with the front quad and glute visibly tensed and engaged. The person faces forward with weight distributed through the front foot, creating a stable asymmetrical stance.

exercises.name: Lateral Band Walks
exercises.pose_description: Standing in a quarter-squat position with a resistance band looped around the ankles or just above the knees. Feet are shoulder-width apart with knees bent and hips hinged slightly. Steps are taken laterally, leading with one foot and following with the other, maintaining constant tension on the band. The torso stays upright and the knees do not cave inward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure stands in a wide quarter-squat stance with one leg fully extended laterally while the other remains bent, creating maximum horizontal separation between the feet and maximum tension on the resistance band. The torso remains upright and centered, knees stay aligned over toes (no inward collapse), and the glutes, hip abductors, and quadriceps are visibly engaged and contracted as the stepping leg reaches its furthest lateral position. The person faces forward with shoulders level and square to the camera.

exercises.name: Seated Shoulder Press
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with back supported and feet flat on the floor. Dumbbells or a resistance band are held at shoulder height with elbows bent and palms facing forward. The arms press straight overhead until fully extended, then lower back to shoulder height. The back remains against the chair and the core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright with their back firmly against the chair, arms fully extended overhead with elbows locked straight, dumbbells or resistance band held at arm's length above shoulder width. The shoulders are elevated and engaged, pressing upward, while the core appears braced with the torso stable and vertical. The face looks forward with visible tension through the shoulders, upper back, and triceps.

exercises.name: Overhead Tricep Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with one arm raised overhead and the elbow bent, dropping the hand behind the head and between the shoulder blades. The opposite hand gently pushes the elbow further behind the head, deepening the stretch along the back of the upper arm. The torso remains tall and the head stays in a neutral position.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with their torso tall and shoulders level. One arm is raised overhead with the elbow bent at approximately 90 degrees, the hand dropped behind the head toward the upper back, while the opposite arm is bent and positioned to gently press the raised elbow further back, creating visible tension through the triceps and posterior shoulder. The head remains neutral, aligned with the spine, and the person's gaze is directed straight ahead.

exercises.name: Standing Chest Fly with Band
exercises.pose_description: Standing with a resistance band anchored behind at chest height, holding one end in each hand. Arms start extended out to the sides at shoulder height with a slight bend in the elbows. The arms sweep forward in an arc, bringing the hands together in front of the chest, squeezing the pectorals. The torso remains upright and stable.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms bent at approximately 90 degrees, crossed in front of the chest with hands meeting near the centerline, elbows slightly lower than shoulder height. The chest muscles appear fully contracted and engaged, with the shoulders drawn slightly forward and the upper back rounded inward from the pectoral squeeze. The torso remains stable and vertical with no rotation.

exercises.name: Diaphragmatic Breathing
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. One hand rests on the upper chest and the other on the belly just below the ribcage. During inhalation, the belly rises prominently while the chest remains relatively still. During exhalation, the belly falls inward. The breathing is slow, deep, and controlled through the nose.
exercises.end_pose_description: Person lies supine with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees and feet flat on the floor, shoulders relaxed against the ground. The abdomen is maximally expanded and visibly distended outward, while the chest remains relatively stationary, with the hand on the belly lifted slightly upward by the rounded, expanded midsection. The face is relaxed looking upward, neck neutral, with deep abdominal and core muscles visibly engaged to support the full inhalation.

exercises.name: Pec Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing beside a doorframe or wall. One arm is placed against the surface with the elbow bent at 90 degrees at shoulder height. The body rotates away from the anchored arm, opening the chest until a stretch is felt across the pectoral muscle and front of the shoulder. The feet are staggered for stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands in a staggered stance facing away from a doorframe, with their torso rotated open to approximately 45 degrees. Their anchored arm remains bent at 90 degrees against the frame at shoulder height, while their chest is visibly expanded and opened, with the pectoral muscles stretched taut across the front of the shoulder and chest. The head is turned slightly to follow the body rotation, creating a gentle twist through the spine.

exercises.name: Double Leg Calf Raise
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart, lightly holding a wall or railing for balance. Both heels rise simultaneously as high as possible, pushing up onto the balls of the feet. The knees remain straight, the body is tall, and the calf muscles fully contract at the top of the movement.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body is fully upright and vertical, balanced on the balls of both feet with heels lifted as high as possible off the ground, creating a visible arch through the foot. The legs are completely straight with no knee bend, the torso is tall and neutral, and the calf muscles are visibly contracted and bulging along the back of the lower leg from the ankle to below the knee. The person faces forward with one or both hands lightly touching a wall or railing for minimal balance support.

exercises.name: Single Leg Calf Raise
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the other foot lifted off the ground, holding a wall or railing for balance. The heel of the standing foot rises as high as possible, pushing up onto the ball of the foot. The knee remains straight, the body stays tall, and the calf muscle fully contracts at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall and upright on the ball of one foot with the heel lifted as high as possible, creating a straight vertical line from hip to the ball of the foot, while the opposite leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and held slightly out to the side for balance. The standing leg's knee remains fully extended and locked, the torso stays erect without leaning, and the calf muscle of the supporting leg appears fully contracted and defined. The hand lightly touches the wall or railing for stability as the body faces forward.

exercises.name: Seated Toe Taps
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. The toes lift off the floor while the heels remain planted, then the toes tap back down. The movement alternates between feet or both feet tap simultaneously, working the tibialis anterior and ankle dorsiflexors in a rhythmic motion.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright in the chair with knees bent at 90 degrees, while the toes are maximally lifted off the floor with the balls of the feet raised as high as possible, creating a pronounced dorsiflexion angle at the ankles. The heels stay firmly planted on the ground, and the tibialis anterior muscles along the front of the shins appear visibly contracted and engaged. The torso remains stable and upright against the chair back.

exercises.name: Standing Hamstring Curl
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding onto a chair or counter for balance. One heel curls upward behind the body toward the buttock by bending the knee, engaging the hamstring. The thighs remain parallel, the standing leg is straight with a slight knee bend, and the torso stays upright without leaning forward.
exercises.end_pose_description: The exerciser stands upright facing forward with the standing leg nearly straight and slight knee bend, while the working leg is bent at approximately 90 degrees with the heel pulled up toward the glutes, creating a sharp knee angle. The hamstring of the bent leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the torso remains perfectly vertical without any forward lean, and both hands maintain light contact with the chair/counter for balance.

exercises.name: Prone Hamstring Curl
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin. One heel curls toward the buttock by bending the knee against resistance from an ankle weight or band. The hips remain pressed into the floor, the thigh does not lift, and the movement is controlled in both the curling and lowering phases.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone (face down) with their torso flat against the ground and forehead resting on folded arms. The working leg's knee is maximally flexed (bent approximately 90 degrees or more), with the heel drawn close to the buttock, while the opposite leg remains fully extended. The hamstring of the bent leg appears visibly contracted and engaged, the hip stays pressed flat to the floor without lifting, and the person faces downward toward the ground.

exercises.name: Wall Squat with Ball
exercises.pose_description: Standing with an exercise ball or stability ball placed between the mid-back and a wall. Feet are shoulder-width apart, positioned about two feet in front of the body. The body lowers into a squat by bending the knees to approximately 90 degrees while the ball rolls along the wall. The back stays pressed into the ball and the knees track over the toes.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a deep squat position with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, thighs nearly parallel to the ground, while their back remains firmly pressed against the stability ball that has rolled down the wall. Their torso is upright and stable, feet are planted shoulder-width apart pointing forward, and their quadriceps, glutes, and core muscles are visibly tensed and engaged. The person faces directly forward with a neutral head position.

exercises.name: Hip Hinge
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart and knees slightly bent. The torso hinges forward from the hips, pushing the buttocks backward while keeping the back flat and chest proud. The arms hang naturally or a dowel rod is held along the spine to maintain spinal alignment. The movement stops when the torso reaches approximately parallel to the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is bent forward at the hips with their torso nearly parallel to the ground, knees slightly bent, and buttocks pushed backward, while the spine remains neutral and straight from head to tailbone. The arms hang straight down or along a dowel rod on the back, and the hamstrings and glutes appear visibly engaged and tensioned. The head remains neutral in line with the spine, and the person's gaze is directed slightly downward.

exercises.name: Quadruped Rocking
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. The hips push backward toward the heels in a rocking motion, sitting back as far as comfortably possible while the hands remain on the floor. The spine stays neutral and the movement is slow and rhythmic, stretching the hips and lower back.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated back on their heels in a deep hip flexion position, with arms extended forward and straight, hands still planted on the floor, creating a long diagonal line from the extended arms through the neutral spine. The hips are maximally retracted toward the heels, knees remain bent at approximately 90 degrees, and the head stays neutral with the gaze directed downward, with visible lengthening through the lower back, lats, and shoulders.

exercises.name: Seated Trunk Rotation
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with feet flat on the floor and knees bent at 90 degrees. A stick, band, or the arms crossed over the chest provide a reference. The torso rotates to one side as far as comfortably possible, then returns to center and rotates to the other side. The hips and knees remain fixed forward while the rotation comes from the thoracic and lumbar spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The seated figure is rotated maximally to one side with the torso twisted at approximately 45-90 degrees from center, while the hips and lower body remain square to the front with feet flat and knees bent at 90 degrees. The arms are either crossed over the chest or holding a stick/band parallel to the shoulders, pointing perpendicular to the direction the torso faces. The oblique and spinal rotator muscles on the rotating side appear engaged and shortened, while those on the opposite side appear lengthened and stretched.

exercises.name: Standing Back Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with feet hip-width apart and hands placed on the lower back for support. The torso gently leans backward, extending the lumbar spine while the hips push slightly forward. The head follows the natural curve of the spine, looking upward, and the knees remain straight. The movement is slow and controlled.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is arched backward at maximum extension with the torso creating a pronounced backward curve from the hips upward, chest lifted and thrust forward, head tilted back following the spinal curve, and both arms bent with hands pressing firmly against the lower back. The hips are thrust slightly forward as an anchor point, legs remain straight with knees locked, and the entire anterior chain (chest, abs, hip flexors) appears stretched and lengthened while the erector spinae muscles along the back are visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Prone Scapular Retraction
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with arms at sides, palms facing down toward the thighs. The shoulder blades squeeze firmly together and downward, lifting the chest slightly off the floor. The forehead may remain on the floor or lift slightly, and the arms lift a few inches off the ground as the scapulae retract. The lower body stays relaxed.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone with their chest lifted noticeably off the floor, shoulders pulled back and down with scapulae maximally retracted, creating visible tension across the upper back and between the shoulder blades. The arms are extended straight or nearly straight at the sides, lifted a few inches off the ground with palms facing down, while the head remains neutral or slightly lifted, and the lower body stays flat and relaxed against the floor.

exercises.name: Seated Cervical Retraction
exercises.pose_description: Seated in a chair with good upright posture, shoulders relaxed, and feet flat on the floor. The chin draws straight backward in a horizontal motion, creating a double chin, without tilting the head up or down. The movement retracts the cervical spine, strengthening the deep neck flexors. The gaze remains level throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person sits upright with their head pulled straight back horizontally, chin tucked inward creating a pronounced double chin, while the gaze remains forward and level. The neck and upper back muscles are visibly engaged and contracted, with the cervical spine in full retraction. The shoulders remain relaxed and level, the spine maintains neutral alignment, and feet stay flat on the floor.

exercises.name: Isometric Cervical Extension
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with one or both hands clasped behind the head. The head pushes backward into the hands with sustained effort while the hands resist the movement, creating an isometric contraction of the neck extensors. No visible movement occurs, the spine remains tall, and the eyes look straight ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with spine tall and neutral, head positioned centrally with eyes looking straight ahead, both hands clasped firmly behind the head at the base of the skull with elbows spread wide to the sides. The neck extensors appear visibly engaged and tense as the head pushes isometrically backward into the clasped hands, creating visible muscular tension in the posterior neck and upper trapezius without any forward or backward head movement.

exercises.name: Isometric Cervical Flexion
exercises.pose_description: Standing or seated upright with one hand placed on the forehead. The head pushes forward into the hand with sustained effort while the hand resists the movement, creating an isometric contraction of the deep neck flexors. No visible movement occurs, the spine remains tall, and the chin stays level.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with their spine tall and chin level, their right hand (or left, depending on variation) pressed firmly against their forehead with the elbow bent at approximately 90 degrees, while their head pushes isometrically forward into the resisting hand creating visible tension in the anterior neck without any actual head movement. The opposite arm hangs naturally at the side, and the engaged deep neck flexor muscles appear taut along the front and sides of the neck.

exercises.name: Wrist Pronation and Supination
exercises.pose_description: Seated or standing with the elbow bent at 90 degrees and held at the side, or the forearm resting on a table. Holding a light hammer or weight, the forearm rotates so the palm turns face down (pronation) and then face up (supination). The elbow remains stationary and the movement is isolated to the forearm rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The forearm is fully pronated with the palm facing downward and the hammer/weight pointing toward the ground, or fully supinated with the palm facing upward and the hammer/weight pointing toward the ceiling. The elbow remains bent at 90 degrees and locked at the side of the body, with visible tension in the forearm flexors and extensors at the end range of rotation. The upper arm and torso remain completely still, isolating the movement to the rotated forearm.

exercises.name: Open Book Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with hips and knees bent to approximately 90 degrees stacked on top of each other. Both arms start extended in front at shoulder height, palms together. The top arm opens upward and rotates across the body like a book opening, reaching toward the floor on the opposite side while the knees remain stacked. The gaze follows the moving hand, creating a deep thoracic rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with hips and knees stacked at 90-degree angles, while their top arm extends fully open across their body with the palm facing upward, reaching toward the floor behind them in a wide arc. Their torso is rotated toward the ceiling with their chest and shoulders opening maximally, their head turned to follow the extended arm, creating a visible stretch across the chest, shoulders, and upper back. Their lower body remains perfectly still and stacked, anchoring the stretch while the obliques and serratus anterior appear engaged to control the rotation.

exercises.name: Prayer Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneeling on the floor, sitting back on the heels with the torso folded forward and the chest resting on the thighs. Arms extend forward on the floor overhead with palms down, and the forehead rests on the floor. The hips stay pressed back toward the heels, creating a long stretch through the lower back, lats, and shoulders.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a compressed forward fold with knees bent and glutes pressed firmly toward heels, while the torso is folded completely forward with the chest resting on the thighs and forehead touching the floor. The arms are fully extended overhead with palms flat on the floor, creating a long line from the fingertips through the spine, with shoulders internally rotated and rounded forward. The person faces downward toward the floor, with the back of the body creating a gentle arch from extended arms through the rounded spine to the compressed hip fold.

exercises.name: Superman Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with arms extended overhead on the floor and legs straight behind. Both arms and both legs simultaneously lift off the floor, arching the back and engaging the erector spinae and glutes. The head lifts with the chest and the gaze is directed at the floor. The position is held briefly at the top with the body forming a shallow U shape.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone with arms fully extended overhead and legs straight, both lifted several inches off the ground, creating a shallow U-shaped arch through the torso. The chest, arms, and thighs are elevated while the pelvis remains as the lowest point, with the head held neutral and gaze directed downward. The erector spinae along the spine and glute muscles are visibly contracted, creating definition along the back and posterior chain.

exercises.name: Swimmers Exercise
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with arms extended overhead and legs straight behind. The opposite arm and leg lift simultaneously — right arm with left leg, then left arm with right leg — in an alternating flutter motion as if swimming. The torso remains relatively still, the head stays in line with the spine, and the movements are small and controlled.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down in a prone position with one arm extended overhead at approximately 160-170 degrees and the opposite leg lifted 6-12 inches off the ground, both fully extended and straight, while the other arm and leg remain lowered, creating a diagonal opposition line through the body. The torso stays relatively flat against the ground, the head remains neutral in line with the spine facing downward, and the engaged back muscles (erector spinae, latissimus dorsi) and glutes on the lifted side appear visibly contracted.

exercises.name: Band Pull-Aparts
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, Scapular Stabilizers & Posterior Shoulder
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with arms extended in front at shoulder height, holding a resistance band with both hands slightly closer than shoulder-width apart. The hands pull the band apart by driving the arms outward and squeezing the shoulder blades together until the band touches the chest. The elbows stay straight and the shoulders remain depressed throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with both arms extended directly out to the sides at shoulder height, elbows locked straight, and the resistance band stretched across the chest touching or nearly touching the torso. The shoulder blades are visibly retracted and squeezed together, creating prominent definition across the upper back and rear deltoids, with the chest slightly expanded and shoulders pulled down away from the ears.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Shoulder Rotations with Band
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, External Rotators & Shoulder Stability
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling position with one knee on the floor and the opposite foot flat in front, hip and knee at 90 degrees. A resistance band is anchored to the side, and the working arm is bent at 90 degrees at the elbow with the elbow at the side. The forearm rotates outward against the band and returns inward, training external rotation. The torso remains tall and the core is engaged.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in half-kneeling position with torso upright and squared forward, while the working arm is rotated outward so the forearm points away from the body at approximately 90 degrees of external rotation at the shoulder, with the elbow still bent at 90 degrees and tucked at the side. The resistance band is fully stretched, creating visible tension across the front of the shoulder and chest, with the rotator cuff and shoulder stabilizers visibly engaged.

exercises.name: Lower Back Release Roll
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back with a foam roller positioned horizontally under the lower back just above the pelvis. Knees are bent with feet flat on the floor. The body gently rolls the foam roller up and down over the lumbar muscles by bending and straightening the legs, applying moderate pressure. Hands may be behind the head or crossed on the chest.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their back with knees fully bent and feet flat on the floor, positioned close to the glutes, while the foam roller is rolled to its highest point under the lower back, creating maximum lumbar extension and arch in the spine. The lower back muscles appear stretched and engaged as the body weight presses into the roller, with hands either supporting behind the head or resting on the chest, and the gaze directed upward toward the ceiling.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Raises
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff, Scapular Stabilizers & Lower Trapezius
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or a bench with arms hanging down. The exercise cycles through three arm positions: I (arms lift straight overhead in line with the body), Y (arms lift at 45 degrees forming a Y shape), and T (arms lift straight out to the sides at 90 degrees). Thumbs point up, shoulder blades squeeze together, and the forehead stays on the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone on the floor with their forehead resting down, shoulders fully retracted with prominent shoulder blade engagement visible along the upper back. Arms are lifted to shoulder height in one of three positions—either straight overhead in line with the body (I position), at 45-degree angles forming a Y shape, or extended directly out to the sides at 90 degrees (T position)—with elbows straight, thumbs pointing upward, and the entire upper back musculature visibly contracted and defined.

exercises.name: Quadruped Shoulder Taps
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips, or in a high plank position. One hand lifts off the floor and taps the opposite shoulder, then returns to the ground. The movement alternates sides. The hips remain level without rocking side to side, and the core is braced to prevent rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: One arm is bent at the elbow and crosses the body to tap the opposite shoulder, while the supporting arm remains straight and locked beneath the shoulder, with the body held in a rigid plank position parallel to the ground. The hips and shoulders remain level and square, showing strong engagement through the obliques and core stabilizers, with the torso resisting any rotation despite the asymmetrical arm position.

exercises.name: Bird Dog Hold with Scapular Punch
exercises.target_area: Core Stability, Rotator Cuff & Scapular Control
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees with right arm extended forward and left leg extended behind, parallel to the floor, in a standard bird dog position. From this hold, the extended arm performs a scapular punch by protracting the shoulder blade forward, pushing the hand further away from the body, then retracting back. The spine remains neutral and the core is fully braced.
exercises.end_pose_description: The athlete is in a quadruped position with the right arm fully extended forward and slightly protracted, with the shoulder blade pushed forward away from the torso, while the left leg remains extended straight behind parallel to the floor. The core, glutes, and shoulder stabilizers are visibly engaged with a rigid, neutral spine, and the person faces downward toward the ground with their gaze neutral.

exercises.name: Bird Dog with Core Stability Focus
exercises.target_area: Core stabilizers, hip extensors, lower back endurance
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists directly under shoulders and knees under hips. The right arm extends forward and the left leg extends behind, both parallel to the floor, with an emphasis on maintaining a perfectly level pelvis and neutral spine. The movement is slow and deliberate with a prolonged hold at full extension, core braced throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a straight line from the extended right fingertips through the torso to the extended left heel, both limbs parallel to the floor at shoulder and hip height respectively, while the supporting left arm and right knee remain vertically aligned beneath the shoulders and hips. The core muscles are visibly tensioned, the pelvis is perfectly level with no rotation, and the spine maintains neutral alignment with the head in line with the extended arm. The person's torso is parallel to the ground with no sagging or hiking of the hips.

exercises.name: Dead Bug with Shoulder Reach
exercises.target_area: Core Stability, Lower Back & Shoulder Integration
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with arms extended straight toward the ceiling and both hips and knees bent to 90 degrees. As the opposite arm and leg extend outward (one arm overhead, opposite leg straight), the reaching arm pushes further toward the ceiling with a scapular protraction, adding a shoulder reach component. The lower back stays pressed firmly into the floor.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their lower back pressed flat against the floor, one arm extended overhead (nearly parallel to the ground) while the opposite leg extends straight out at hip height, creating a long diagonal line through the body. The reaching arm shows pronounced shoulder protraction with the scapula visibly lifted off the ribcage, while the core, obliques, and stabilizer muscles are clearly engaged to maintain the extended position and spinal stability.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms resting at sides with palms down. The hips press upward by squeezing the glutes until the body forms a straight line from shoulders to knees. The weight is driven through the heels, and the core remains engaged at the top.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with shoulders and head remaining on the ground, hips thrust upward to create a straight diagonal line from knees through torso to shoulders. Knees are bent at approximately 90 degrees with feet flat on the floor, arms pressed into the ground at the sides with palms down for stability. The glutes, hamstrings, and lower back are visibly contracted and engaged, with the pelvis tilted upward and core muscles tight.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge with Isometric Hold
exercises.target_area: Gluteal muscles, hip extensors, lower back
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms at sides. The hips are lifted to the top position forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, and this position is held isometrically for a sustained duration. The glutes are maximally squeezed, the core is braced, and the hips do not drop.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with hips thrust upward in a straight diagonal line from shoulders to knees, creating a bridge position where the torso is elevated and parallel to the ground. The knees remain bent at approximately 90 degrees with feet flat and hip-width apart, while the glutes appear maximally contracted and tightened, the core is visibly braced, and the shoulders remain flat against the floor. The arms rest at the sides with palms down, and the face points upward toward the ceiling with the body creating a strong horizontal platform from knees to shoulders.

exercises.name: Half-Kneeling Pallof Press
exercises.target_area: Core, Lower Back Stabilization & Rotational Control
exercises.pose_description: In a half-kneeling position with the inside knee down and the outside foot forward, positioned perpendicular to a cable or band anchor point. Both hands hold the band or cable handle at the chest. The arms press straight forward, extending fully away from the chest, resisting the rotational pull of the band. The torso remains perfectly upright and square, the core braces against rotation.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a half-kneeling position with arms fully extended straight forward at shoulder height, elbows locked, gripping the cable handle with both hands pressed away from the chest. The torso remains perfectly vertical and squared forward with no rotation, core visibly braced, while the back and oblique muscles appear engaged in resisting the lateral pull of the cable. The head remains neutral facing forward, shoulders packed and stable.

exercises.name: Lateral Side-Lying Clam Shell
exercises.target_area: Gluteus medius, hip external rotators, trochanteric bursa
exercises.pose_description: Lying on one side with hips bent to approximately 45 degrees and knees bent to 90 degrees, feet stacked together. The bottom arm extends under the head, and the top hand rests on the hip. The top knee opens upward like a clamshell while the feet stay together and the pelvis remains stable without rolling backward. A resistance band may be placed just above the knees.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies on their side with the top knee opened maximally upward (approximately 70-90 degrees), creating a wide angle between the two knees while the feet remain pressed together and the pelvis stays stable without rotating backward. The hip and glute muscles on the upper side are visibly engaged and contracted, while the lower body maintains its 45-degree hip bend and 90-degree knee bend position.

exercises.name: Lying Hip Flexor Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying on back at the edge of a bed or table with both knees pulled to the chest. One knee remains hugged to the chest while the other leg lowers off the edge, hanging down toward the floor with the knee slightly bent. Gravity pulls the lowered thigh into extension, stretching the hip flexors and front of the thigh. The lower back stays flat on the surface.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with their torso flat against the bed/table surface. One leg is pulled toward the chest with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees, while the opposite leg hangs off the edge of the surface with a slightly bent knee, creating a deep stretch through the extended hip and anterior thigh. The lower back remains in contact with the surface, and the stretched leg's thigh is in full extension with the knee maintaining a gentle bend.

exercises.name: Prone Glute Squeeze Holds
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms at sides or folded under the forehead. Both glute muscles are maximally squeezed together and held in a sustained isometric contraction. The legs remain on the floor, the hips press gently into the floor, and the contraction is held for several seconds before releasing.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains prone and motionless on the floor, face down with legs fully extended and straight behind them, arms positioned at sides or folded beneath the forehead. Both glute muscles are visibly tensed and contracted, creating a firm, rounded appearance in the buttocks region, while the hips maintain gentle contact with the floor and the entire lower body appears locked in rigid isometric tension.

exercises.name: Prone Hip Extension Pulse
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down with legs extended straight and arms folded under the chin. One leg lifts a few inches off the floor with the knee straight, then performs small pulsing movements upward, rapidly contracting the glute at the top of each pulse. The hips remain pressed into the floor and the leg does not touch down between pulses.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies face-down on the floor with their forehead resting on folded arms, one leg extended straight and raised to its maximum height (approximately 8-12 inches off the ground) with the knee locked straight, while the opposite leg remains extended on the floor. The glute of the raised leg appears visibly contracted and engaged at the peak of the pulse, with the hips firmly planted against the floor and no rotation in the torso.

exercises.name: Prone I-Y-T Shoulder Activation
exercises.pose_description: Lying face down on the floor or an incline bench. The arms cycle through three positions with controlled holds: I (arms extended straight overhead close to the ears), Y (arms lifted at 45 degrees from the head), and T (arms lifted straight to the sides at 90 degrees). Thumbs point up, the shoulder blades squeeze together, and each position is held for a few seconds before transitioning.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies prone (face down) with their forehead resting on the mat, arms fully extended overhead at one of three positions: either straight up by the ears (I position), at 45-degree angles from the body (Y position), or directly out to the sides at 90 degrees (T position). The thumbs point upward, the shoulder blades are visibly squeezed and retracted toward the spine, and the upper back and rear deltoids appear engaged and lifted slightly off the ground.

exercises.name: Quadruped Hip Flexor March
exercises.target_area: Hip flexors, core stabilizers, lower back
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. One knee lifts slightly off the floor, driving the thigh upward in a marching motion while the hands remain planted. The movement alternates legs in a slow marching pattern. The spine remains neutral, the hips stay level, and the core is braced to prevent shifting.
exercises.end_pose_description: The performer is in quadruped position with one thigh driven upward to approximately hip height, knee bent at roughly 90 degrees, while the opposite leg remains extended and planted on the ground. The torso remains parallel to the ground with a neutral spine, shoulders stacked over wrists, and the pelvis stays level and square without rotation—the abdominals appear visibly engaged and braced. The lifted knee hovers several inches above the floor while the supporting arm and leg create stable anchor points.

exercises.name: Quadruped Pelvic Tilts
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips. The pelvis tilts posteriorly by tucking the tailbone under and rounding the lower back slightly, then anteriorly by arching the lower back and tilting the tailbone upward. The movement is isolated to the lumbar spine and pelvis while the upper back and shoulders remain still.
exercises.end_pose_description: From a side profile view, the person is in quadruped position with arms vertical and legs at 90-degree angles. The lower back is maximally arched with the tailbone pointed upward, the pelvis tilted anteriorly, and the chest lifted slightly forward—the abdominal muscles appear relaxed while the lower back extensors and hip flexors are visibly engaged. The head maintains neutral alignment following the spine's natural curve, and the shoulders remain stable directly over the wrists.

exercises.name: Resistance Band External Rotation at 90/90
exercises.target_area: Rotator Cuff (Infraspinatus & Teres Minor) & Shoulder Stability
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright with the working arm abducted to 90 degrees and the elbow bent to 90 degrees, forming a goalpost position. A resistance band is anchored at elbow height. The forearm rotates upward from a position pointing down toward the floor to a position pointing toward the ceiling, externally rotating the shoulder while maintaining the 90/90 arm position. The elbow stays at shoulder height throughout.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with their working arm held at 90/90 position (shoulder abducted 90 degrees, elbow bent 90 degrees), and the forearm has externally rotated upward so it points toward the ceiling, creating a goalpost shape with the upper arm remaining parallel to the ground. The opposite arm hangs naturally at their side, and the torso remains stable and upright with visible engagement in the shoulder rotators and upper back musculature.

exercises.name: Single-Leg Balance with Hip Activation
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly soft and the hip of the standing leg actively engaged. The non-standing leg lifts with the knee bent and the hip moves through small ranges of flexion, extension, or abduction to challenge balance. Arms may be at sides or on hips, the torso is upright, and the gaze is fixed on a point ahead.
exercises.end_pose_description: The camera captures a figure standing tall on one straight leg with the standing hip and glute visibly engaged and stable, while the non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and the hip abducted, extended, or flexed to its endpoint depending on the movement pattern. The torso remains upright and vertical with no lateral lean, the core appears engaged and tight, and the gaze is directed straight ahead at a fixed point.

exercises.name: Standing Single-Leg Balance with Hip Stability
exercises.target_area: Hip stabilizers, gluteus medius, proprioception, lower back
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg with the standing knee slightly bent, focusing on keeping the pelvis level without dropping on the unsupported side. The non-standing leg is lifted with the knee bent to approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion. Arms are at sides or on hips, the torso is tall, and the gluteus medius of the standing leg is actively engaged to maintain pelvic stability.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands tall on one leg with a slightly bent knee, maintaining a perfectly level pelvis without any lateral drop, while the opposite leg remains lifted with the knee bent at approximately 90 degrees of hip flexion and positioned in front of the body. The torso is upright and centered over the standing leg's foot, with visible tension through the glutes and hip stabilizers of the standing side, while the arms are either relaxed at the sides or resting on the hips, and the gaze is fixed forward.

exercises.name: Supine Figure-4 Stretch with Pelvic Mobilization
exercises.target_area: Piriformis, gluteal muscles, hip external rotators
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with one ankle crossed over the opposite knee in a figure-four position. Both hands reach through and clasp behind the thigh of the bottom leg, pulling it toward the chest. Additionally, the pelvis gently rocks side to side in small mobilization movements, enhancing the stretch through the piriformis and outer hip of the crossed leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with the left ankle crossed over the right knee in a tight figure-4 position, while both hands clasp firmly behind the right thigh, pulling it toward the chest with the right knee bent at approximately 90 degrees and drawn close to the torso. The pelvis is tilted at its maximum lateral rotation point (either left or right side slightly lifted), creating a deep stretch visible through the tensed piriformis and glute muscles of the crossed leg, with the head and shoulders remaining flat against the ground.

exercises.name: Supine Iliopsoas Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back at the edge of a bed or table. One knee is pulled to the chest and held with both hands, while the other leg hangs off the edge of the surface, allowing gravity to extend the hip and stretch the iliopsoas. The thigh of the hanging leg drops below the surface level, and the lower back remains flat.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine on their back with one knee pulled tightly to their chest (hip and knee flexed at approximately 90 degrees), held by both hands, while the opposite leg hangs vertically off the edge of the surface with the hip extended and knee slightly bent, creating a deep stretch through the front of the hip and thigh. The lower back remains pressed flat against the surface, the torso is stable and centered, and the hanging leg's thigh drops noticeably below the horizontal plane of the bed or table.

exercises.name: Supported Cat-Cow Stretch
exercises.target_area: Lower Back, Thoracic Spine & Shoulder Mobility
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees with a yoga block or cushion under the hands for wrist support, or with forearms on a chair seat for reduced wrist loading. The spine alternates between arching downward with the chest lifting and belly dropping (cow) and rounding upward with the chin tucking and tailbone curling under (cat). The movements are slow and synchronized with breathing.
exercises.end_pose_description: At the peak of the cat phase, the spine is maximally rounded with the upper back arched toward the ceiling, shoulders hunched upward, chin tucked toward the chest, and tailbone curled under; the arms remain straight or slightly bent (supporting on hands or forearms depending on modification), knees are bent at 90 degrees on the ground, and the entire posterior chain from neck to pelvis appears engaged and contracted upward. The head hangs naturally with gaze directed downward, and the abdominal muscles are visibly engaged as the torso forms an inverted U-shape.

exercises.name: Quadruped Thoracic Rotation
exercises.target_area: Intercostal muscles, thoracic spine, obliques, chest
exercises.pose_description: On hands and knees in tabletop position. One hand is placed behind the head with the elbow pointing out to the side. The torso rotates, driving the elbow toward the opposite hand on the floor (closing), then rotates upward, driving the elbow toward the ceiling (opening). The hips remain square over the knees and the rotation occurs through the thoracic spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in quadruped position with the torso rotated maximally upward, the elbow that was behind the head now pointing toward the ceiling with the arm bent at approximately 90 degrees, while the gaze follows the elevated elbow. The opposite arm remains extended and planted on the floor, supporting the body weight, while the hips stay square and aligned over the knees with no rotation. The thoracic spine shows pronounced rotation and extension, with the ribcage visibly twisted open and the chest facing toward the elevated side.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.target_area: Obliques, transverse abdominis, anti-rotation core stability
exercises.pose_description: Standing perpendicular to a cable machine or band anchor point with feet shoulder-width apart and knees slightly bent. Both hands hold the handle or band at the center of the chest. The arms press straight forward, extending fully, resisting the rotational pull of the band. The core is fully braced, the hips remain square, and the torso does not rotate.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands perpendicular to the cable machine with both arms fully extended straight forward at chest height, creating a 90-degree angle between the torso and extended arms. The core appears braced and rigid with the torso facing forward, shoulders square, and hips locked in place without any visible rotation despite the cable tension pulling laterally. The obliques and rectus abdominis are visibly engaged and tightened, resisting the rotational force.

exercises.name: Glute Bridge Hold
exercises.target_area: Glutes, lower back extensors, core stabilizers
exercises.pose_description: Lying flat on back with knees bent at approximately 90 degrees, feet flat on the floor hip-width apart, arms at sides. The hips are pressed upward into the bridge position, forming a straight line from shoulders to knees, and this position is sustained for the prescribed duration. The glutes remain fully contracted, the core is braced, and the hips do not drop throughout the hold.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person lies supine with their upper back and shoulders firmly planted on the ground, hips thrust upward in a straight, level line parallel to the ground, creating a bridge shape from shoulders to knees. The knees are bent at 90 degrees with feet flat and hip-width apart, while arms rest at the sides with palms down. The glutes and lower back are visibly contracted and engaged, forming a taut, elevated line across the torso and thighs.

exercises.name: Child's Pose with Side Reach
exercises.target_area: Lower back, intercostal muscles, latissimus dorsi
exercises.pose_description: Kneeling with the torso folded forward in a child's pose position, forehead resting on or near the floor. Both arms are extended forward on the floor, then both hands walk to one side, creating a lateral stretch through the side of the torso, lats, and intercostals. The hips stay pressed back toward the heels, and the stretch is felt along the opposite side of the body.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains in a deep kneeling position with hips pressed back toward heels, torso folded forward and laterally flexed, with both arms extended diagonally across the floor toward one side and forehead resting on or near the ground. The entire body creates a curved line from the extended arms through the torso to the knees, with the ribcage and lateral core visibly elongated on the stretched side while the opposite side appears compressed.

exercises.name: Banded Shoulder Stabilizer Series
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright holding a resistance band with both hands. The exercise cycles through multiple positions: band pull-aparts at chest height, external rotation with elbows at sides, overhead press against band tension, and diagonal patterns. Throughout each movement, the shoulder blades are actively set down and back, the core is engaged, and the posture remains tall and aligned.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright facing forward with shoulders pulled back and down, arms extended outward at shoulder height with the resistance band stretched wide across the chest, elbows slightly bent, and chest expanded with visible engagement through the upper back and rear deltoids. The core appears braced, spine neutral, and the entire posterior chain from shoulders through glutes shows tonal engagement against the band tension.

exercises.name: Downward Facing Dog
exercises.pose_description: Starting from hands and knees, the figure pushes hips up and back into an inverted V shape. Arms are straight and extended overhead pressing into the floor, head between the upper arms looking toward the feet. Legs are straight with heels pressing toward the ground. Back is flat forming a straight line from hands to hips.
exercises.end_pose_description: The body forms a perfect inverted V-shape with the head positioned between fully extended arms, eyes gazing down toward the feet planted on the ground. The hips are pushed high and back, creating a straight diagonal line from the hands through the torso to the heels, with legs fully extended and shoulder blades drawn down the back, visibly engaging the core and shoulder stabilizers.

exercises.name: Lat Stretches
exercises.pose_description: Standing upright, the figure reaches one arm overhead and leans to the opposite side, creating a long stretch along the side of the torso from hip to fingertips. The other arm hangs naturally at the side. Feet are shoulder-width apart with a slight lateral bend in the torso.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure stands upright with feet shoulder-width apart, one arm stretched fully overhead with the elbow straight, while the torso leans deeply to the opposite side creating a pronounced C-curve from the hip through the extended fingertips. The opposite arm hangs relaxed at the side, and the latissimus dorsi and oblique muscles along the stretched side appear lengthened and engaged, with the figure's gaze following the overhead arm.

exercises.name: Lateral Lunge with Reach
exercises.pose_description: The figure takes a wide step to one side, bending that knee while keeping the other leg straight. The torso leans slightly forward and the opposite arm reaches toward the bent knee foot. The straight leg inner thigh is stretched. Weight is on the bent leg with the foot flat on the ground.
exercises.end_pose_description: The figure is in a deep lateral lunge position with the torso upright or slightly forward-leaning, the bent knee (on the lunging side) flexed to approximately 90 degrees with foot flat on the ground, while the opposite leg remains fully extended and straight behind or to the side. The arm on the side opposite the bent knee extends forward and across the body toward or past the bent knee's foot, with the shoulder rotated inward, while the torso shows visible engagement through the obliques and lateral core. The head faces forward in the direction of travel, and the weight is centered over the bent leg.

exercises.name: Quadriceps Sets (Isometric)
