exercises.end_pose_description: The person stands upright with one leg fully extended and locked straight, knee joint completely contracted with the quadriceps visibly tensed and hardened. The opposite leg remains slightly bent in a supporting position, with the torso upright and stable, facing forward with arms relaxed at the sides or slightly forward for balance.

exercises.name: Copenhagen Adduction
exercises.pose_description: Side-lying on the floor with the top leg resting on a bench or elevated surface. The bottom leg is hanging free beneath the bench. The person lifts the bottom leg up toward the bench by squeezing the inner thigh (adductors). The upper body is propped on the forearm in a side plank position. The top leg stays on the bench for support.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is in a side-lying position with the bottom leg lifted and pressed firmly against the top leg, creating a closed adductor squeeze where both legs are nearly parallel and stacked. The torso remains elevated on the forearm in a side plank, with the body forming a relatively straight line from head to knees, while the inner thighs visibly contract and engage. The person faces forward along the length of their body, with the bench supporting the top leg as the bottom leg reaches its maximum height at hip level.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Seated on the floor with one leg bent 90 degrees in front (shin parallel to shoulders, knee pointing outward) and the other leg bent 90 degrees behind (shin pointing backward). Torso upright, hands on the floor for light support. Hips open, gentle forward lean over the front shin.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person is seated with their torso folded forward over the front leg, chest approaching or touching the front shin while maintaining the 90/90 leg configuration (front shin parallel to shoulders with knee splayed outward, back shin pointing straight back). The spine is rounded in flexion, shoulders are internally rotated and drawn forward, and the hamstrings, glutes, and hip external rotators of the front leg appear fully engaged and stretched. The person's gaze is directed downward toward the front knee.

exercises.name: Couch Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Kneeling on one knee with the back foot elevated against a wall or couch behind. Front leg is bent at 90 degrees with foot flat on the floor. Torso tall and upright, hands on the front knee for balance. Deep stretch visible in the hip flexor and quadriceps of the back leg.
exercises.end_pose_description: The torso is leaned back with the chest open and shoulders back, creating an extended arch through the spine while the back knee remains planted and the back foot pressed against the wall/couch behind. The front leg stays bent at 90 degrees with foot firmly planted, while the hip flexors and quadriceps of the back leg are maximally stretched and visibly engaged. The head is in neutral alignment or slightly back, and the hands may release from the front knee as the core stabilizes the extended position.

exercises.name: Seated Posture Micro-Practice
exercises.pose_description: Seated upright in a chair with feet flat on the floor. Spine tall and neutral, shoulders rolled back and down, chin slightly tucked. Hands resting on thighs. Demonstrating ideal seated posture alignment with a subtle glow or highlight along the spine.
exercises.end_pose_description: The person remains seated upright with spine fully extended and neutral, shoulders actively drawn back and down creating visible scapular retraction, chest lifted and open, chin parallel to the ground with a subtle tuck, and hands resting naturally on the thighs with arms at roughly 90-degree angles. The entire posterior chain—erector spinae, rhomboids, and upper back muscles—appears engaged and highlighted, with the torso forming a vertical line from the crown of the head through the pelvis. The person faces directly forward with eyes ahead, feet planted flat on the floor hip-width apart.

exercises.name: Standing Hip Flexor and Quad Stretch
exercises.pose_description: Standing on one leg, the other foot pulled behind toward the glutes with one hand gripping the ankle. The standing leg is slightly bent. Free arm extended to the side for balance. Hips pushed slightly forward to emphasize the hip flexor and quad stretch. Relaxed posture suggesting an evening cooldown.
exercises.end_pose_description: The standing leg remains slightly bent while the stretched leg is pulled up behind the body with the knee deeply flexed (approximately 90 degrees), foot drawn close to the glutes with the hand firmly gripping the ankle. The torso is upright with a slight forward pelvic tilt, the free arm extended out to the side for balance, and the person faces forward with a relaxed, neutral expression. The hip flexors and quadriceps of the back leg appear fully lengthened and engaged in the stretch.
